# X module (`odyssey.so`) functions read in full, one entry each

Release IRIX 6.5.30m, `usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so` (N32, `$gp` resolved with `ghidra/scripts/IrixGp.java` before reading). Each entry names the function, its address in the module and its size in bytes. Labels are **established** for functions whose whole listing was read next to the decompilation, and **inferred** for anything less. The role lists of the whole module are in [odyssey-so-functions.md](odyssey-so-functions.md). Offsets such as +0x1b4 in a screen record are the X server's own `ScreenRec` and window-record fields; the module keeps two screen-private slots, the board record (`odsyScreenPrivateIndex`) and the video-control record (`vcScreenPrivateIndex`).

## Segment and glyph paths

- `_odyDebugf..MD` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 968 bytes): **established.**
  A variadic debug-print routine starting at 0x1666d90. It saves its argument registers to the stack (`sw` at 0x1666d94, `sd` at 0x1666d98 through 0x1666dac and 0x1666db4) in a 1104-byte frame and reads two words, at gp+0x48 (0x173aa08; `lw` at 0x1666db0) and gp+0x4c (0x173aa0c; `lw` at 0x1666dc4). When the word at gp+0x48 is not positive (`blez` at 0x1666dbc) it continues at 0x1667088; otherwise, when the word at gp+0x4c is zero (`beq` at 0x1666dc8) it returns at 0x1667070 without printing.
  Both printing cases call `sprintf` into the stack buffer: the positive case with the format at 0x172e428, the string at 0x172e438 and the word at gp+0x48 (`jalr` at 0x1666de0), the other case with the format at 0x172e448 (`jalr` at 0x1667098). Both then call `vsprintf` (`jalr` at 0x1666fcc) with the caller's format string and the saved variadic arguments, and `ErrorF` (`jalr` at 0x1667068) with the format at 0x172ce48 and the stack buffer. Between the calls, byte loops store 0x20 and read the buffer; which bytes they pad and compare is **unknown**. The routine writes no board state. The GOT entries at gp-28520 and gp-27716 are the slots of `sprintf` and `vsprintf`.

- `odsySegmentSD` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 9832 bytes): **established.**
  The complete routine starts at 0x1587b50. It derives a segment mode from the drawable and visual records, clears the pending-board word at +0x1cb8 (`sw` at 0x1587cd4), and emits the common settle words through the FIFO pointer (`sw` at 0x1587ce4, 0x1587cf0, 0x1587cfc and 0x1587d10). It stores the selected line state at +0x84 of the context (`sw` at 0x15880cc), dispatches modes below 12 through a table loaded from the module data (`jr` at 0x15880d4), and otherwise calls the mode helper with the mode in its second argument (`jalr` at 0x1588100). The mode bodies update the packed line fields at +0xbc, +0xc0 and +0xc4 (`sw` at 0x158a0d8, 0x158a0f4 and 0x158a110), then write those three words to the FIFO after token 0x10c21 (`sw` at 0x158a154, 0x158a160 and 0x158a16c). Each completed path clears the four cached words at +0x2b44 through +0x2b5c of the drawable record (`sw` at 0x158a180, 0x158a188, 0x158a190 and 0x158a198) before returning through 0x15887c8 or 0x15887ec. The segment body was read from 0x1587b50 through 0x158a1b7; the mode-specific line encoding is established, while the board meaning of the packed fields remains unknown.
- `odsySegmentSS` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 7732 bytes): **established.**
  The complete routine starts at 0x158fc70. It selects a line mode from the drawable state, writes the resulting flags to context +0x84 (`sw` at 0x15901bc), and sends the helper's mode through the indirect call at 0x15901e8. Its mode bodies use the line-style byte at +0x48 of the selected record to set or clear the high flag (`lbu` at 0x1590228 and `or` at 0x1590254), combine the endpoint and mode fields into a packed command word (`sll` at 0x1590260 and 0x1590268, then `and` at 0x1590270 and 0x1590274), and send the resulting state through the FIFO pointer after the pending word at +0x1cb8 is cleared (`sw` at 0x1590874). The routine has separate branches for the supported mode values and returns through 0x1590838 or 0x159085c; the final drawable cleanup clears +0x2b44, +0x2b4c, +0x2b54 and +0x2b5c (`sw` at 0x1591a74, 0x1591a7c, 0x1591a84 and 0x1591a8c). Its listing, 0x158fc70 through 0x1591aa3, was read in full. The software's packed line fields are established, but their hardware interpretation is unknown.
- `odsyPolyGlyphBltTE6` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 12968 bytes): **established.**
  The complete TE6 path starts at 0x1596740. It prepares the glyph drawing state and repeatedly sends the settle prefix through the FIFO pointer, including token 0x10443 and its wait operand (`sw` at 0x1596c8c, 0x1596c98, 0x1596ca4 and 0x1596cb0), then copies the glyph source words into packed output records. The packing loop reads 16-bit glyph values from the source streams (`lhu` at 0x15998b0, 0x15998b4, 0x15998dc and 0x15998e8), keeps their top ten bits with mask 0xfc00 (`andi` at 0x15998bc, 0x15998c0, 0x15998ec and 0x15998f4), shifts them into one output word (`dsll` at 0x15998c4, 0x15998d0, 0x15998f0 and 0x15998fc), and stores each packed record through the stack cursor (`sd` at 0x15999a4). It advances the source cursors by two bytes per glyph word (`addiu` at 0x15998a0, 0x15998a8, 0x15998c8 and 0x15998e0), loops until the source end, and restores the saved context before returning through 0x1597240 or 0x1597274. Every instruction from 0x1596740 through 0x15999e7 was read; the glyph-to-pixel bit orientation is unknown.
- `odsyPolyGlyphBltTE8` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 12016 bytes): **established.**
  The complete TE8 path starts at 0x15999f0. It follows the same state and FIFO setup as the TE6 path, but its glyph packing loop consumes the source as bytes within 16-bit loads: the terminal bytes are masked with 0xff00 (`andi` at 0x159c81c, 0x159c820, 0x159c838 and 0x159c848), shifted into separate byte positions (`dsll` at 0x159c828, 0x159c830, 0x159c844 and 0x159c854), combined with the other source bytes (`or` at 0x159c83c, 0x159c858, 0x159c880 and 0x159c898), and written as an 8-byte packed record (`sd` at 0x159c8c0). The loop advances each source cursor by two bytes (`addiu` at 0x159c7e4, 0x159c7ec, 0x159c808 and 0x159c810), repeats until the cursor reaches the end pointer (`beq` at 0x159c8bc), and leaves the glyph cell state set to one halfword (`sh` at 0x159a4dc) before returning through 0x159a50c or 0x159a540. The bytes of 0x15999f0 through 0x159c8df were read in full; the byte packing is established and the board's interpretation of the pattern remains unknown.
- `odsyPolyGlyphBltTE9` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 13004 bytes): **established.**
  The complete TE9 path starts at 0x159c8e0. It packs the glyph-cell geometry into the drawable record (`sh` at 0x159ca6c, 0x159ca70, 0x159ca74 and 0x159ca80), derives the two 12-bit cell bounds (`andi` at 0x159ca78 and 0x159caa0), and stores them at +0x2b40 and +0x2b44 (`sw` at 0x159ca88 and 0x159cab0). It clears the remaining drawable completion pairs (`sw` at 0x159cab4, 0x159cabc, 0x159cac4 and 0x159cac8), sends the pending FIFO settle group after testing +0x1cb8 (`beqz` at 0x159cad0 and `sw` at 0x159cad8), and packs source halfwords using mask 0xff80 (`lhu` at 0x159fad0, 0x159fad8, 0x159fae8 and 0x159faec; `andi` at 0x159fae4, 0x159faf4, 0x159fafc and 0x159fb00). The packed words are written through the output cursor (`sd` at 0x159fb7c), with helper calls at 0x159cc18 and 0x159d0a0 before the epilogues at 0x159d4c8 and 0x159d4fc. The packing loop from 0x159c8e0 through 0x159fba8 was read in full; the source bit packing is established, while the board's glyph interpretation remains unknown.
- `odsyZeroPolyArc` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 21672 bytes): **established.**

## Stub and one-line routines

- `odsyInitAllocator` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1694d40, 8 bytes): **established.**
  Reports success without doing any work: the listing is two instructions, `jr ra` at 0x1694d40 and `li v0,1` in its delay slot at 0x1694d44, and no state is read or written.
- `odsyQueryMaxSwapBarrier` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1636cf0, 8 bytes): **established.**
  Also returns 1 and nothing else, through `li v0,1` at 0x1636cf4 behind the return at 0x1636cf0; it does not read its arguments or the board record, and no limit is written for the caller.
- `odsyInstallFakeColormap` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x163f030, 8 bytes): **established.**
  Does nothing: `jr ra` at 0x163f030 and a no-op at 0x163f034, and no argument is read.
- `odsyStoreFakeColors` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1623c70, 8 bytes): **established.**
  Returns at once: the return is at 0x1623c70 with a no-op delay slot at 0x1623c74, and no argument or global is read or written.
- `odsyWakeupHandler..M` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x158f8f0, 8 bytes): **established.**
  Returns at once: the whole routine is the return at 0x158f8f0 and the no-op after it at 0x158f8f4, so it reads and writes nothing.
- `rrmUndoubleBufferWindow` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x161bda0, 8 bytes): **established.**
  Returns at once: the routine is `jr ra` at 0x161bda0 followed by a no-op at 0x161bda4 and reads or changes no window or board state.
- `odsyScanAudioInventory..K` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15931e0, 36 bytes): **established.**
  Tests one record: when the word at +4 of the first argument is 10 it stores 0 through the second argument and returns 1 (`li v0,1` at 0x1593200, the delay slot of the `jr ra` at 0x15931fc), otherwise it returns 0 at 0x15931f4 and stores nothing.
- `odsySetColor` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16ffb80, 56 bytes): **established.**
  Guard against a call that must not happen: it prints "odsySetColor: should not be called." with `ErrorF` (the call at 0x16ffba0) and returns; it sets no colour and touches no board register.
- `odsyInitWindowType` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1631730, 80 bytes): **established.**
  Stores the window type halfword of the window's resource-manager private (at +2): it is 1 when the window's frame-buffer-layer private has a nonzero word at +0x18 (branch at 0x1631768, store at 0x1631774) and 0 otherwise (store at 0x163177c). The two private records are found through `rrmWindowPrivateIndex` and `nfbWindowPrivateIndex` in the window's private array at +0x84.
- `rrmNeedCID` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1586c00, 96 bytes): **established.**
  Returns 0 or 1 from two stored numbers. It loads the screen's resource-manager record word at +8 and the object at +0x34 of the first argument; with no object it answers 0 when that screen word is nonzero and 1 when it is zero (branch at 0x1586c50), and with an object it answers 1 when the screen word is below the object's word at +4 (the compare at 0x1586c3c) and 0 otherwise.

## Screen controls, genlock and timing-file output

- `odsySetScrnGlock` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x169c100, 120 bytes): **established.**
  Records the screen's genlock source. The third argument must be -1 or -2 (the two values `setmon` passes to the input-sync call, -2 for its external source); any other value prints "odsySetScrnGlock: Invalid sync source: %d" with `ErrorF` (the call at 0x169c134) and the value is not stored, while a valid one is stored at +0x18 of the video-control screen record by the delay-slot store at 0x169c168.
- `odsySetExternalLock..GD` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x165a130, 72 bytes): **established.**
  Selects which external lock input the screen follows. The second argument is stored at +0x30 of the video-control screen record only when it is not negative and is below the record's count at +0x2c (the branches at 0x165a150 and 0x165a160, the store at 0x165a16c); an out-of-range number is ignored without a message.
- `odsyGenlockHandler..FD` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15ff550, 92 bytes): **established.**
  Handler run when genlock status changes. It stores its second argument at +0x1c of the video-control screen record (the store at 0x15ff58c), calls `odsyBlankScreen` with mode 0 and the screen at 0x15ff590, and returns 0.
- `odsyQryCntrl..JD` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16de370, 140 bytes): **established.**
  Answers a control query for one screen. For control 10 it writes 0 at +0x20 of the reply block; for control 5 it converts the integer at +0x7c of the board's screen record to a float stored at +0x10 of the reply (the `cvt.s.W` at 0x16de3e8); for control 11 it tests the bit selected by the second argument in the mask at +0x134 of the board record and writes 1 or 0 at +0x28 of the reply (the stores at 0x16de3cc and 0x16de3f8); every other control returns with the reply untouched.
- `odsyWriteTTfilename` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x169c180, 176 bytes): **established.**
  Writes the three-line timing-table file that `setmon` also writes: it opens the path in the first argument for writing (the call to `fopen` at 0x169c1a0; a failure returns 10), then prints the format name with "%s" and the two integers (the colour depth and the accumulation type) each with "%d" and a newline, closes the file and returns 0.

## Timing and format-file routines

- `odsyLoadTimingTable..CC` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x170a7f0, 5308 bytes): **established.**
  Builds the 320-byte video timing structure of the kernel's timing-table request from a video format file and loads it (arguments: screen, format-file handle, format record, a flag to enable the timing generator afterwards, genlock source; result 1 on success, 0 on any failure). Read as the whole 1327-instruction listing next to the decompilation, `$gp` = 0x173a9c0. The names below are resolved through the module's constant-pool slot at 0x17339b8 (base 0x172acc0); each is read from the file with `SDBgetSymbolValueScalar` into a stack word and every miss prints "odsyGetScalar: unable to find %s" with `ErrorF` and returns 0, after freeing the two table buffers. The structure is the stack block at sp+0x28, offsets below are from its start.
  Set-up. The routine keeps the file descriptor from the screen's second-level record (the pointer at +0x74, word +100) and the board record from the screen private slot `odsyScreenPrivateIndex`. It clears the structure with `bzero(…, 0x140)`, stores the caller's genlock source at +220, the refresh rate (the float at format-record +0x110, truncated) at +184 and the fields-per-frame word (format-record +0x12c) into +172, and clears the flag word at +200. ## Compositor routines

All compositor register writes go through `odsyCmpIoctl` as a request whose first byte is 0xaa (the two-wire address byte with bit 0 clear, a write), second byte the register number and word +4 the data. "Register n" below means that write. Unless stated, a failed write prints "Failure writing to compositor" and ends the routine.

- `odsyCompositorExternalWrite..KC` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1711bc0, 252 bytes): **established.**
  Writes one register of a device behind the compositor's own two-wire master (arguments: screen, device address, register, value; result 0, or -1 with "Error writing external compositor reg"). It writes compositor register 0x55 three times with the data (device address and 0xff) or 0x1300, then (register and 0xff) or 0x1200, then (value and 0xff) or 0x1a00. The three halves are the address, the sub-register and the data of the external device.

- `odsyProgramCompositors..GC` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15af3a0, 276 bytes): **established.**
  Numbers every open compositor (no arguments; returns 0). It walks the module's 32-entry table of compositor links (80 bytes per entry, descriptor at +8 of the entry) and for each entry with a positive descriptor sends a 20-byte request with `ioctl(descriptor, 0x636d7004, request)`: word 0 is 0x14, word 1 is 1 (a write), word 2 is 1, word 3 is 0x5a (the register) and word 4 is the one-based entry number shifted left 8. A failure prints "odsyProgramCompositors ioctl error: %s" with `strerror` and the walk continues.

- `odsyQueryCompositors..DC` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1636a70, 304 bytes): **established.**
  Finds the compositor devices the operating system offers (no arguments; result the number of open links, or -1 when the module's count at 0x173b418 is already nonzero). It opens the directory "/hw/compositor", skips names that start with a dot, converts each name with `atoi`, and for numbers 0 to 31 opens "/hw/compositor/%d" read-write; a descriptor above zero goes into entry n of the table (at +0x58 from the table start, 80 bytes per entry, so entry n sits where `odsyCmpIoctl` finds compositor number n+1) and the count is incremented. The directory is closed before the count is returned.

- `odsyPowerSaver..IE` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x163d150, 244 bytes): **established.**
  Screen-saver callback that blanks and restores the display (arguments: screen pointer, mode; result 0, 1 or 3). Mode 0 returns 0 and does nothing. Mode 1 clears the screen's saver flag (a word per screen at 0x173f330 + 4 times the screen number) with `odsyBlankScreen(0, screen)` when it was set, and returns 0. Mode 3 returns 1 when the flag is already set and 0 when the saved screen record's byte at +8 is 2; otherwise it calls `odsyBlankScreen(2, screen)`, sets the flag and returns 1. Any other mode returns 3.

- `odsySetCompositorTiling..PC` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16ad200, 1200 bytes): **established.**
  Programs the compositor's four tile windows from a combination record (arguments: screen, combination record; result 1 on success, 0 on a failed write). It first clears bit 5 of the control shadow at +0x84 of the board-private record and writes it to register 0. Then, for tile k from 0 to 3, it reads the four words at combination offsets 0x310 + 16k to 0x31c + 16k (a, b, c, d) and writes register 0x23 + k with ((c divided by 4, rounding toward zero) shifted left 16 and masked to 0x03ff0000) or ((a divided by 4) and 0x3ff), then register 0x27 + k with (b and 0xfff) or ((d shifted left 16) and 0x0fff0000). The order is 0x23, 0x27, 0x24, 0x28, 0x25, 0x29, 0x26, 0x2a. It ends by writing the shadow with bit 5 set to register 0.

- `odsySetupCompositorInfo` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1623210, 2648 bytes): **established.**

  Reading (first part). For each open compositor in the table of links (80 bytes per entry, `gp` - 0x1a78 up, count at 0x173b418) a read request goes through `ioctl(descriptor, 0x636d7004, request)`: word 0 is 0x14, word 1 is 0 (a read), word 2 is 3, word 3 the register and the data comes back in word 4. The first string (the manufacturer) is skipped. The second (the product name) is read byte by byte and right-aligned in a 14-byte field padded with spaces. The third (the serial number) is right-aligned in a 9-byte field, and its first six characters are also copied to a short field. The fourth (the part number) is right-aligned in an 18-byte field with each underscore replaced by a hyphen. The fifth (the dash level) is right-aligned in a 6-byte field. Afterwards ten bytes behind the dash level take 0x30 with two 0xff markers. A failed read prints "Failure reading NIC board offset: %s", "manufacturer", "product name", "serial number", "part number" or "dash level" (the same text with that item) with `strerror(oserror())`, sets the entry's error word to 1 and goes on to the next compositor.

## Board control routines

- `odsySetCntrl..ID` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16a56d0, 492 bytes): **established.**
  Sets one screen control (arguments: screen, head, control number, value block; no result). The kernel descriptor is word +0x64 of the record at +0x74 of the screen. Control 10 stores 0 at +0x20 of the value block and returns. Control 5 reads the float at +0x10 of the block: below 1.0 it stores 0 at +0x7c of the board-private record, otherwise 1, and sends the word with `ioctl(fd, 0x6f640023, &private+0x7c)` (the kernel's DAC gain request; failure prints "odsyEnableVTG: ODSY_BRDMGR_SET_DAC_GAIN Failed '%s'"). Control 11 acts only for the last head (the video-control record's word +4 minus one) on a board whose record word +0x1d0 is nonzero: it sends a 48-byte two-wire request (halfword 1 at +0, command 16 at +2, device byte 0x9b at +6, port 1, 4 bytes with the word 1 when the block's word at +0x28 is nonzero and 0 otherwise) through `ioctl(fd, 0x6f640021, request)`; a failure prints "odsy DM5 blanking: ioctl failed: %d" and ends. On success bit n of the mask at +0x134 of the board record (n the head) is cleared and set again when the block's word +0x28 is nonzero (the mask `odsyQryCntrl..JD` returns for control 11). Every other control number returns without action.

- `odsySetChannelInputRectangle..IC` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x156f690, 500 bytes): **established.**
  Moves the input window of the option card's second channel (arguments: screen, head, then the new x and y as floats; no result). It acts only when the head is the last one and the board record's word at +0x1d0 is nonzero. The head entry's width (+0x10) and height (+0xc) are read; x and y are clamped to at least 0 and so that the rectangle stays inside the screen (halfwords at +8 and +10 of the screen). The DM5 chip is then written through `ioctl(fd, 0x6f640021, request)` with a 48-byte two-wire request (command 16, device byte 0xa9, port 1, 16 bytes holding the high byte and the low byte of x, then of y, one in each word). A failure prints "SetChannelRect: ioctl failed. %d". On success the entry's +4 holds x, +8 holds y and +0xc and +0x10 are rewritten with the height and width.

- `odsyDisplayInit` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16d9fa0, 532 bytes): **established.**
  Programs the board's window-id display modes at screen start (argument: screen; no result). The per-screen table of window modes (480 bytes per screen, the pointer stored at +0x58 of the board-private record) is cleared. The record's word at +0x10 indexes a word table at 0x1738228: a value of 8 selects the 25-row mode table at 0x1738248 and 16 the 29-row table at 0x1738378 (the pointer is saved in the module's word at 0x173b41c). Each row holds a window id, a flag and a display-mode word; the three words are copied into the screen's table at 12 bytes per window id and sent with `ioctl(fd, 0x6f64001d, {id, mode})` (the kernel's display-mode request). A failure prints "odsyDisplayInit: ODSY_SETDISPLAYMODE ioctl failed" and "wid = %d, mode = 0x%x, errno = %d" and the loop goes on. Every row then calls `rrmSetReservedDID(screen, id, flag, mode)`. At the end bit 5 is set in the halfword at +0x528 of the resource-manager screen record. The tables list window ids 0 to 19 and 0x20 to 0x24, and the larger table 0 to 0x17 and 0x20 to 0x24; each of the ids 0 to 7 has flag 0, ids 8 to 13 flag 1 and the ids from 0x20 up flag 0x3c00 with the mode words 0xa1, 0xa9, 0xb1, 0xbb and 0xc3.

- `odsySetFBConfig..KD` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16081e0, 832 bytes): **established.**
  Changes the frame-buffer depth or the accumulation-buffer type and records it in the timing-table file (arguments: screen, what to change, request block; result 0, 1, 2, 10 or the result of the file write). It builds the path "/var/X11/Xvc/Odyssey%d_TimingTable" and reads the current name, depth and accumulation type with `odsyReadTTfilename` (a result of 3 prints "unable to create or read file '%s'" and returns 10). What to change 0 sets the depth from word 0 of the block: on a board whose words at +0x18 and +0x28 are 2 and 0 a depth of 16 with a format name starting "1280x1024_60" prints "16 byte framebuffer depth not supported" and "with 1280x1024_60* video format." and returns 1; a depth other than 8 or 16 (the two-entry table at 0x1738240) prints "Invalid framebuffer depth '%d'" and returns 2. What to change 1 takes the accumulation type from word 1 of the block: 0 and 1 are accepted, anything else prints "Invalid accumulation buffer type '%d'" and returns 2. After an accepted change the size of the current format comes from `odsyGetDimensionsFromTTFile` and, when that succeeds, a probe request goes through `ioctl(fd, 0x6f64001b, {width, height, depth, accumulation, 1})`; a nonzero answer prints "memory oversubscribed by the selected configuration" and returns 1. The file is written with `odsyWriteTTfilename` (failure prints "unable to write '%s'.") and its result is returned. Any other value of the first selector only writes the file.

- `odsyKernInit..O` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15ce820, 780 bytes): **established.**
  Starts a board's kernel side at screen set-up (arguments: screen, a word handed on to `irixKernInit`, a pointer to a word placed in the attach request, a pointer to the kernel descriptor; result 1, or 0 after any failure). Read as the whole listing. It calls `irixKernInit` for the screen (a zero result returns 0), then configures the frame buffer with `ioctl(descriptor, 0x6f64001b, request)` where the request holds the board-private record's words at +0x18 and +0x1c, the word of the table at 0x1738228 that the record's +0x10 selects, the record's +0x14 and a zero (no probe); a failure prints "odsyKernInit: ODSY_BRDMGR_CONFIG_FB failed" and returns 0. The five reply words are stored in the record at +0x20 to +0x34. The module keeps a pointer array of 32 per-board state regions (the array of 0x80 bytes is allocated on first use); the board number at record +0x5c must be below 32 ("Number of boards larger than allowed"). For a board without a region it prints "attaching for brdnum=%d", allocates 0x2e80 bytes aligned to 0x4000 ("cannot allocate buzz state region" on failure), clears them and sends the memory-attach request `ioctl(descriptor, 0x6f640000, request)` with -1 in word 1, the word the third argument points to in word 2, the region address at +0x10 and 0 at +0x18; a failure prints "odsyKernInit: ODSY_MM_ATTACH failed", frees the region and clears the table entry. On success the reply fields at +0x18 and +0x20 of that block are stored in the region at +0x2b7c and +0x2b78. Finally the configure reply words at +0x14 and +0x18 go to record +4 and +8.

- `odsyLoadCmap` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16f0ec0, 708 bytes): **established.**
  Loads a colour-map change into the board (arguments: screen, request block; no result). The block holds a count in its first halfword and a pointer at +0xc to 8-byte entries of an index and a packed colour (three 10-bit components in bits 29:20, 19:10 and 9:0). First every entry's colour word is stored into the board-private record's shadow table (the pointer at +0x54, four bytes per index). When the screen has a video-control colour record (`XSGIvcScreens[screen]`), every entry whose index is below 0x1900 is then corrected through the tables that the record's pointer chain (+0x24, then +0xc) leads to: each 10-bit component v is widened to 12 bits as ((v shifted left 2) or (v shifted right 8)) and compressed to a table index (the value itself below 0x200, 0x100 plus half of it below 0x400, otherwise 0x200 plus a quarter), and the 16-bit table entry is looked up at index times 2 in a table of 0x600 entries; the component in bits 29:20 uses the table at +0, bits 19:10 the one at +0xc00 and bits 9:0 the one at +0x1800, and the new colour word is (first result shifted left 14 and masked to 0x3ff00000) or (second shifted left 4 and masked to 0xffc00) or (third shifted right 6 and masked to 0x3ff), written back into the entry. Finally, when the word at +0x13c of the board-private record equals 1, the block is sent with `ioctl(fd, 0x6f64001a, block)` (the kernel's colour-load request); a failure prints "odsyLoadCmap: cmap load error".

## Cursor and gamma routines

In this section and the four after it, **established** means the decompilation was read in full and the listing was checked at every address and constant the entry cites; **inferred** marks an entry where the listing was checked less, and the entry says which parts.

- `odsyLoadGamma0` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1609d70, 624 bytes): **established.**
  Loads an all-zero gamma ramp and, when a video-control record exists for the screen, blanks the ordinary colour map as well (argument: the screen; no result). It reserves a 0xf810-byte block on the stack (a zero result at 0x1609dc0 prints "odsyLoadGamma0:  couldn't allocate memory" and returns) and builds a colour-load request in it: a count of 0x1f00 in the first halfword (0x1609dc8) and the entry array at +0x10, 8 bytes an entry (index, packed colour). The first 0x600 entries are written in the order the loop at 0x1609df0 enumerates the compressed ramp index (the sample value runs 0 to 0x1ff one at a time, then 0x200 to 0x3ff in steps of 2 and 0x400 to 0xfff in steps of 4, and the entry number is the sample for the first range, half of it plus 0x100 for the second and a quarter of it plus 0x200 for the third), each with index 0x1a00 plus that entry number (the addiu at 0x1609e00) and colour 0: the 0x600-entry gamma ramp at colour-map index 0x1a00 that `docs/buzz.md` places at `odyssey.c:467-483`. The other 0x1900 entries (the loops at 0x1609eb0) carry indices 0 to 0x18ff, each with the current colour from the board-private record's shadow table (the pointer at +0x54). The routine then writes every entry's colour back into that shadow table (0x1609f00 to 0x1609f28): the gamma indices are zeroed in the shadow and the ordinary ones are rewritten with their own values. If the screen has a video-control record (the slot at `vcScreenPrivateIndex`, tested at 0x1609f2c), the colour of every entry whose index is below 0x1900 is set to 0 in the request only (the store at 0x1609f68), after the shadow copy, so the shadow keeps the real colours. The request goes to the kernel with `ioctl(descriptor, 0x6f64001a, block)`, the descriptor being the word at +100 of the structure behind screen +0x74, and a nonzero result prints "odsyLoadGamma0: cmap load error". Unlike `odsyLoadCmap`, it does no table correction and never tests the board word at +0x13c. The reading that this blanks the display is **inferred** (a zero ramp and, with video control, all-zero colours; nothing in the routine names its caller's purpose).
- `odsyInstallCursor` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1605c90, 704 bytes): **established.**
  Programs one cursor image and position on the board (arguments: the realized cursor record, hotspot x, hotspot y, screen). It sends the kernel's cursor request `ioctl(descriptor, 0x6f64001c, block)` (kernel `gfP_OdsyBRDMGRcursor`, flag meanings in `docs/display.md`, "Kernel cursor request") five times, each with the flag in the block's first word and its own failure message. (1) Flag 4 with the control word at +0x44 of the board-private record and bit 1 cleared: the cursor is switched off while the image changes ("ODSY_SET_CONTROL ioctl failed"). (2) Flag 0x30, glyph pointer at block +0x18 equal to the buffer pointer at +8 of the cursor record and alpha pointer at +0x20 equal to that buffer plus 0x200, which is the 512-byte glyph part followed by the 256-byte alpha part that `odsyDisplayCursor` fills ("ODSY_CURSOR_SET_GLYPH ioctl failed"). (3) Flag 4 again: when the halfword at +0x3e of the structure behind record +0x5c is 1 and bit 4 of the control word is set and the video-control record's object at +8 exists, bit 5 of the control word is set if the float at +0x1fc of that object is not above the global pointer position `coreX`, and cleared otherwise; without that condition bit 5 is cleared; either way bit 1 is cleared (the test at 0x1605d98 and the compare at 0x1605eec). I read bit 4 as dual-head enabled and bit 5 as pointer on the second head (**inferred**; the control word's bit meanings are unknown in `docs/display.md`). (4) Flag 4 with bit 0 set. The stored word then gets bit 0 cleared and bit 1 set, so bit 0 is the transient switch-on request and bit 1 the module's record that the cursor is shown, as in `odsyCursorOn`. (5) Flag 3 with word 1 holding the hotspot (x in the high half, y in the low half) and word 2 the pointer position from `coreX` and `coreY` in the same packing.
- `odsyDisplayCursor` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x168afc0, 2368 bytes): **established** for the control flow and request sequence, **inferred** for the pixel meaning of the glyph and alpha bits.
  Makes a cursor the current hardware cursor of a screen (arguments: screen, cursor; result 1). The cursor's per-screen record is the word at index screen-number + 5 of the cursor structure (+0x14 onward) and holds a realized flag (halfword +0xc), a pointer at +4 to a record that carries a second colour and a 768-byte buffer pointer at +8. If the cursor is the one the board record already shows (the word at +0x48), only the control sequence is repeated: flag-4 requests clearing bit 1, then setting bit 2 and, under the same dual-head test as `odsyInstallCursor`, bit 5 from the pointer position, then setting bit 0, and a flag-3 position request with hotspot 0 and the pointer position (the sends at 0x168b0e0, 0x168b144, 0x168b194 and 0x168b214; the failure messages name ODSY_SET_CONTROL and ODSY_SET_POS). Otherwise a cursor with no record for the screen returns 1 at once; else bit 2 of the control word is cleared, and if the realized flag is 0 it is set and the buffer is filled from the cursor's source and mask bitmaps (clamped to 32 by 32). Each row takes a 32-bit source word and mask word masked by a left-aligned width mask and writes 16 bytes of glyph (4 bits a pixel) and 8 bytes of alpha (2 bits a pixel, value 3 where the mask is set); the glyph value is 1 and the pixel is expanded through the 16-word table at rodata offset 0xb70, which maps each four-bit group of the source-and-mask word to four nibbles of value 0 or 1 in mirrored order. When the record at +4 is absent or its byte +6 is zero this table path is used; otherwise the loop at 0x168b304 sets glyph value 1 for the first 16 pixels of the row wherever the mask is set and, for the last 16, only where source and mask are both set, with alpha 3 for every mask pixel; why the halves differ is **unknown**. The installed function is then called through the pointer at +0x8c of the structure behind screen +0x74 with the cursor record and the cursor's hotspot halfwords (+0xc and +0xe of the cursor bits), and `odsySetCursorColor..CB` reloads the colour table. Nothing in this routine stores the +0x48 word.
- `odsySetCursorColor..CB` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15e5700, 880 bytes): **established.**
  Builds and sends the cursor's 15-word colour table (arguments: the cursor, the screen; no result). Word 0 comes from the cursor's background colour (halfwords at +0xa, +0xc, +0xe), word 1 from its foreground colour (+4, +6, +8) and word 2 from the second colour that the cursor's per-screen record points to (three halfwords at +0, +2, +4; with no second colour all three components use table index 0). The other 12 words are zero. Each 16-bit X component is shifted right by 4 and compressed to a table index (itself below 0x200, half plus 0x100 below 0x400, a quarter plus 0x200 above), then looked up at index times 2 in the 16-bit table at the end of the video-control record's pointer chain (`XSGIvcScreens[screen]`, +0x24, then +0xc), the one `odsyLoadCmap` uses for red; all three components use this table, not the three per-channel tables of `odsyLoadCmap`. The word is (red entry masked to 0xffc0, shifted left 14) or (green entry masked to 0xffc0, shifted left 4) or (blue entry shifted right 6): red in bits 29:20, green 19:10, blue 9:0. The 60-byte table goes to the kernel as flag 8 with its address at block +0x10 through `ioctl(descriptor, 0x6f64001c, block)`; a failure prints "odsySetCursorColor: ODSY_SET_CMAP ioctl failed, errno = %d". That table word n is the colour of glyph pixel value n (15 entries for values 0 to 14, with 15 having no entry) is **inferred**: it fits the glyph values written by `odsyDisplayCursor` (0 for the background pixels under alpha 3, 1 for the foreground) and the PROM note in `docs/display.md` that value 15 has no entry. That note's reading of the 15 words as the colours of values 1 to 15 is not consistent with this routine.

## Pixel-buffer and hyperpipe routines

- `odsyAllocatePbuffer` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x166d8f0, 1388 bytes): **established.**
  Allocates the board memory behind a GLX pixel buffer and attaches a drawable to it (argument: the pixel-buffer record; result 1, or 0 after any failure, which also releases the group). The record supplies the screen at +0x10, the buffer id word at +4 (`lw` at 0x166dda4), width at +0xc and height at +0xe. It builds a 72-byte memory-allocation request (layout in `docs/opengl.md`): -1 at +0 and +4 (no group yet), object type 0, and a description with byte 0 = 3, byte 1 = 2 shifted left by a size code, sizes at description +16 and +20 equal to the width and height and +24 equal to 1. The size code comes from a table in the board-private record: the entry at +0x50 selected by the GLX window private's word at +0x48 minus the screen record's word at +0x24 when the buffer has no window with a visual, otherwise the 0x44-byte entry at +0x4c selected by the visual (word +0xc of the entry). Byte 15 is 1 when the GLX private's word at +0x54 is 0x18. The request goes out as `ioctl(descriptor, 0x6f640001, block)` at 0x166db30 (kernel `gfP_OdsyMMalloc`); a failure prints "Unable to allocate pbuffer depth %d width %d height %d" (the depth printed is always 16), and a returned group of -1 prints "ODSY_MM_ALLOC didn't fail but we got back an invalid handle". When the reply flag word (+52) has bit 1 set, its value at +56 is stored in the 0x2e80-byte region that `odsyKernInit` made, in the table at region +0x2c00 at the index in the reply halfword at +64. If the GLX private's byte at +0x50 is nonzero and byte 15 is 1, the request is repeated for object types 3 and 4 with byte 1 set to 8, which adds two further objects to the same group (the loop at 0x166daf0; a failure releases the group with `ioctl 0x6f640002`). It then queries slots 0 to 6 of the group (`ioctl 0x6f640004`, "Failed ODSY_MM_QUERY (group) ioctl") and, when reply flag bit 4 is set, stores the reply's value in the region table at +0x2b80 at the index in the halfword 0x20 bytes into the reply (`lhu` at 0x166dcb4). The reply halfwords at +0x10 and +0x12 locate a 16-byte record in that table (chunk number the upper 6 bits, record the lower 10, 0x166dcc4 to 0x166dcf0): the halfword 4 bytes into it is set to the entry of the table at region +0x2b7c plus 1 (`sh` at 0x166dd04) and the halfword 6 bytes into it to 1 (`sh` at 0x166dd0c), and after a `sync` (0x166dd14) the group's slots 0 to 6 are made resident (`ioctl 0x6f640003`, "Failed MakeResident"). The last request, `ioctl 0x6f64002a` with the buffer id and the group, associates the buffer with a drawable ("ODSY_PBUF_ASSOC failed: '%s'" with `strerror`). The kernel entry points and their numbers are in `docs/ioctls.md`.
- `odsyQueryHyperpipeConfig` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x165f7f0, 444 bytes): **established.**
  Fetches the current display-pipe configuration of a screen from the kernel and caches each pipe's name (arguments: screen number, configuration id, a pointer for the pipe count; result a pointer to the module's table of pipe records, or 0 with the count 0). If the compositors have not been opened (`odsyCompositorFDsOpen` zero) and `odsyQueryCompositors..DC` finds some, `odsyProgramCompositors..GC` runs first (0x165f964 to 0x165f980). It sends the 524-byte configuration block with the id at +8 as `ioctl(descriptor, 0x6f640011, block)` (kernel `gfP_OdsyHPgetConfig`), the descriptor being the word at +100 of the structure behind the screen's record in `screenInfo`. A nonzero result stores 0 in the count. On success the count (the first word of the reply) is stored through the third argument, then for every pipe (16-byte entries from block +0xc) the entry's words at +0x10, +0x0c and +0x14 are copied into the module's pipe table (stride 0x5c) and the board-information request `ioctl(descriptor, 0x66, {entry word at +0x18, buffer, 0x28})` fills a 40-byte buffer whose name is copied with `strcpy` into the 0x54-byte name records (the loop at 0x165f8e0 to 0x165f954); a result of -1 calls `perror`, stores 0 and returns 0.
- `odsyQueryHyperpipeNetwork` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1665e00, 712 bytes): **established.**
  Reads the hyperpipe topology and refreshes the module's pipe name table and per-pipe board records (arguments: screen number, a pointer for the pipe count that may be null; result a pointer to the table of name records, 0 on failure). The compositor start-up check is the same as in `odsyQueryHyperpipeConfig`. It sends `ioctl(descriptor, 0x6f640010, block)` (kernel `gfP_OdsyHPgetTopology`, 388-byte result; a failure calls `perror` and stores 0 in the count) and then, for each pipe of the reply (12-byte entries), asks the board-information request 0x66 for the name (40-byte buffer, copied into the 0x54-byte name record) and stores two words of the entry into the module's per-pipe tables. When the caller passes no count pointer it also asks for the full 588-byte record with request 0x66 ("Get board info (long) failed") and stores the record's word at +500 (the compositor word) into the board-information record that `ddxGetBoardInfo` returns for that pipe. After the loop it calls `odsySetupCompositorInfo` and sets the module's network-read flag (the word at 0x173a9f8 is raised to 1 if it was 0, the store at 0x166604c).
- `odsyHyperpipeConfig` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1671c00, 616 bytes): **established.**
  Programs a display-pipe configuration (arguments: screen, configuration id, a pointer that receives the new configuration id, a pointer to the pipe count and the array of pipe name records to use; result 0 after the request, or 0 early for an unknown pipe). It stores -1 in the output word first and starts the compositors as in `odsyQueryHyperpipeConfig` when they are not open. It builds the 524-byte block with the count at +0, the id at +8 and for each requested pipe a 16-byte entry from +0xc holding three words copied from the record's +0x54, +0x58 and +0x50. If the network has not been read (the word at 0x173a9f8 is 0) `odsyQueryHyperpipeNetwork` runs. The record's name is matched with `strcmp` against the module's name table (0x54-byte records; an unmatched name returns 0), and the pipe's identity word from the module's table at 0x1739df8 (indexed by the matched record's position) is stored in the entry at +0x18 and sent with the board-information request 0x66, whose reply buffer is not read (a result of -1 calls `perror` and returns 0). The block then goes to the kernel as `ioctl(descriptor, 0x6f640012, block)` (kernel `gfP_OdsyHPconfig`, which also reprograms the compositor tiling); on success the reply word at +8 is stored in the output, otherwise -1 is stored.

## Platform parameter routines

- `odsySetPltParam` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1685800, 1204 bytes): **established.**
  Applies one platform parameter that a client (`setmon`, the compositor tools) sends to the X module (arguments: screen, unused, parameter id, data size, data pointer; result 0, or 2 for a bad id or size). The id indexes a 0x5d-entry jump table at 0x172a6e0 (an id of 0x5d or more, or any id whose entry is the default, prints "odsySetPltParam: Unknown paramId = 0x%x" and returns 2); the entries I decoded are these, and every other id below 0x5d takes the default. Ids 0 and 1 need a size of 0x20 and call `odsySetFBConfig..KD` with the data. Id 2 needs size 4 and sends the video timing generator control request `ioctl(descriptor, 0x6f640020, {2, value})` ("odsyEnableVTG: ODSY_BRDMGR_VTG_CONTROL Failed"). Id 3 needs at least 4 bytes: it stores the first word at +0x88 of the board-private record and, when that word is nonzero, copies the string that follows into the record at +0x8c and calls `odsyReadPFDArgs..LD` on it. Id 6 needs size 0xc and sends the data through `odsyCmpIoctl` as a compositor register write ("odsy compositor write: ioctl failed."), and id 7 needs size 0xc and only stores its first byte, second byte and halfword 8 bytes in (`lhu` at 0x1685a68) into the record's +0x80, +0x81 and +0x82 (the compositor read request that `odsyQryPltParam` completes). Id 8 needs size 0x30 and passes the data unchanged as a two-wire command to `ioctl 0x6f640021` (kernel `gfP_OdsyBRDMGRi2ccmd`); a negative result prints the command and returns 2, and a nonzero status word at +0xc in the reply prints "status = %d" and returns 2. Ids 9 and 0x5b build a 48-byte two-wire command in the stack from the data and send it with `ioctl 0x6f640021`: id 9 needs size 0x38 and sends command 4 with the word at +0 copied into the command's word 8 bytes in and the low halfword of the word at +4 copied into the command's first halfword, the data pointer set to +9, the count taken from the byte at +0x31 and the low halfword of the word at +0x34 copied as well; id 0x5b needs size 0xa8 and sends command 0x10 with a byte count of four times the first word, the low byte of the word at +4 as the command's byte at +6 and the data pointer set to +8 ("odsy I2C sendbytes platform param: ioctl failed"). Id 0xc needs size 4 and stores its word in the module's word at 0x173aa10; id 0x5c does nothing and returns 0. The names of ids 6 to 9 and 0x5b to 0x5c follow `docs/vpro-tool-functions.md` where its callers are read; the commands' meaning on the wire is **inferred** from the compositor routines in this file.
- `odsyQryPltParam` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15f3e10, 888 bytes): **established.**
  Answers one platform parameter query (arguments: screen, unused, parameter id, data size, data pointer; result 0, or 2 for a failed request, a bad size or an unknown id). For ids 0 and 1 it needs a size of 0x20 and fills the block with the frame-buffer depth from the module's table `bufferDepths` indexed by the board-private record's word at +0x10, the record's word at +0x14, and six floats made from the unsigned words at record +0x20 to +0x34, each multiplied by 2^-20 (the constant at rodata 0x172e164 is 0x35800000); I read the six as 12.20 fixed-point per-screen values (**inferred**; this routine does not name them). Id 7 needs size 0xc: it copies the record's three values at +0x80, +0x81 and +0x82 into the block and runs `odsyCmpIoctl` on it, the read half of the compositor register access ("odsy compositor read: ioctl failed."). Id 10 needs size 0x38 and sends command 3 as a two-wire read (`ioctl 0x6f640021`, "odsy I2C recvbytes platform param: ioctl failed"). Id 0x1f needs size 0xa4 and sends command 0xf with a one-word reply buffer at +4; the reply word is stored at +0 of the data, or 0 on a failure ("odsy I2C vbob platform param: ioctl failed"). Any other id prints "odsyQueryPlatformParam: Unknown paramId = 0x%x" and returns 2; a wrong size prints "odsyQryPltParam: Illegal dataSize = 0x%x".

## Image transfer routines

All five routines below belong to the X module's `PutImage` and `GetImage` paths. The rectangle argument is four 16-bit values (x0, y0, x1, y1), the user buffer is a host address and the stride is in bytes (0 means the row length). Every routine starts by clearing the word at +0x84 of the board's per-board state region (the 0x2e80-byte block that `odsyKernInit` makes) and reads the window's format entry from the 0x44-byte table that the board-private record's word at +0x4c points to, indexed by the window's frame-buffer-layer private word at +0x3c minus the screen record's word at +0x50.

- `odsyReadImage` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1571cb0, 1120 bytes): **established.**
  Reads a rectangle of the window into host memory (arguments: rectangle, host buffer, stride, window; no result). It first writes the FIFO settle sequence that `docs/opengl.md` gives (0x10443 with operand 0xfa, two 0x10046, 0x10019, then 0x10443 with 0x96 and four 0x10046, then 0x10443 with 0xfa, two 0x10046) and the words 0x10658 and 0x120000, clears the halfword at +0x68 of the board-private record, and builds one 80-byte transfer request in the stack for `ioctl(descriptor, 0x6f640006, block)` (kernel `gfP_OdsyMMxfr`, request layout in `docs/kernel.md`, the call at 0x15720b8; failure prints "odsyReadImage: ODSY_MM_XFR pixel transfer failed: '%s'" with `strerror`). Where the entry's fields name hardware pixel-mode bits is **inferred** from `docs/kernel.md`, the shapes only: that table gives the header layout, this routine's masks fill it.

Above `env_dma_threshold` it calls `odsyDrawImageDMA..H`; above `env_pio_threshold` it calls `odsyDrawImagePIO..G`; at or below it, a window of class 0 or 7 (frame-buffer-layer private +0x14) goes to `odsyDrawSmallCI8Image..I` and every other class to `odsyDrawImagePIO..G` (the compares at 0x15ee684 and 0x15ee68c). It then loads parameter-memory constants and tables as `docs/buzz.md` describes for register 0x31 and register 0x34: register 0x31 gets 0x1e0 (word 0x310081e0), then block word 0x9080bda2 with 16 words from region +0x243c: 1.0, 0.5, -1.0, 0, a word computed from a call to `sqrt` with 8.0, 3.0, one from `sqrt` with 2.0, one from a second `sqrt` with 2.0 times 0.25 (stored at +0x2458), then zeros. **The listing converts the integer register v0, not the double result in f0, after each of those three calls** (`mtc1 v0` with `cvt.s.W` at 0x15c67e8, 0x15c680c and 0x15c6844), as if `sqrt` had been declared to return an int. If the shipped `sqrt` leaves v0 untouched (its code was not read here: **unknown**), v0 still holds the 0x20000000 loaded at 0x15c66d8 and the three words are 536870912.0, 536870912.0 and 134217728.0 instead of 2.83, 1.41 and 0.35. **Read in the next passage.** Whether any microcode program reads those three constants is **unknown**: the program table of `ucode/buzz_routines.md` was not searched for readers of parameter-memory words 0x243c to 0x2458 of that register block. Register 0x34 is set to index 0 (word 0x34008000) and gets block word 0x9080bdc8 with a 16-word matrix from region +0x1a10 (rows 1, 0, 0, 0.5; 0, 1, 0, 0.5; 0, 0, 1, 0; 0, 0, 0, 1); it is set to index 0x10 (0x34008010) and gets block word 0x908091df with the 4 words (0, 0, 0, 1.0) from +0x1a50, and is left at index 0. The shadow word at +0x26a0 (register 0x31) is set to 0x141 later, without a send.

Finally it calls `odsyDisplayInit` and `odsyCursorInit` and enables the video timing generator with `ioctl(descriptor, 0x6f640020, {1})`, printing "odsyEnableVTG: ODSY_BRDMGR_VTG_CONTROL Failed '%s'" with `strerror(errno)` on a failure. What each state word selects on the board beyond the names in `docs/words.md` is **unknown**.

## Video format loading routines

- `odsyLoadAndFree` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16ffbe0, 1400 bytes): **established.**
  Applies a chosen video format to one head and releases the format list that selected it (arguments: screen, head number, the format-information array to free, a word passed through, the chosen format record with its name at +0, a load flag; result 0 on success, 2 when the load or the monitor enable failed). The routine is stored in the video-control function table by `odsyAttachXvc`, so its callers are in the Xvc layer. The load flag is the sixth argument. When it is 0 the routine only records the choice: it frees the array, builds the path "/var/X11/Xvc/Odyssey%d_TimingTable" from the screen's number, reads that file with `odsyReadTTfilename` (a result of 3 prints "unable to read or create file"), rewrites it with `odsyWriteTTfilename` using the new format name and the two integers that read returned (a failure prints "unable to write"), and returns 0 without touching the board. This answers the question left open in `odsyLdFmtByName..OC` about the file-mode register: the branch is selected by the sixth argument being zero, and the same shape appears in both routines. With the flag set and no compositor mode (the board record's word at +0x1cc zero, or bits 2:1 of it nonzero, or the head's entry word at +0x1e8 differing from it) it copies the format name, appends ".vfo", builds the database path under "/usr/gfx/ucode/ODSY/vof" with `odsyMakeFileName`, opens it with `SDBreadOpenDatabase` ("Failed to open", result 2) and loads the timing with `odsyLoadTimingTable..CC` using the video-control record's word at +0x18 ("odsyLoadTimingTable Failed", result 2). If the screen is the current one it then calls `odsyCursorOn(1, screen)`. For head 0 and a format whose name differs from the head entry's current one (strcmp against entry +0x14), it frees the entry's old field array at +0x144, copies the 0x138-byte format record into the entry at +0x14, allocates a field array of 0x24-byte records (count at record +300, "Couldn't allocate field info" and result 2 on failure), copies the fields from record +0x130, sets the entry's flag word at +0 to 1 and stores the width and height as floats: 0 at +4 and +8, the record's +0x100 at +0xc and +0x104 at +0x10. When the video-control record's word at +4 is 2 (two heads) the same format is copied to the second head's entry at +0x1f8 + 0x14, whose flag at +0x1f8 is set to 1 and whose words at +0x1fc, +0x200, +0x204 and +0x208 are the record's +0x104 as a float, 0, the record's +0x100 as a float and its +0x104 again; the cursor routines compare the pointer position with the word at +0x1fc to pick the head, so the second head starts at x equal to that value; `odsyAttachXvc` stores the screen width in the first entry's word at +0x10 and half of it as the second entry's word at +4 (dual head), which fixes the entry layout as +4 x origin, +8 y origin, +0xc height and +0x10 width, all floats, and makes the record's +0x104 the head width (**inferred** from that match). In the compositor case it calls `odsyLoadCompositorTiming..LC` instead. All paths that reach the end set `screenIsSaved` to 1 and call `odsyBlankScreen(0, screen)` ("Cannot Enable Monitor" when it fails), free the array and close the database.
- `odsyDefaultTTExists` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16962a0, 4020 bytes): **established** (the whole listing, 0x16962a0 to 0x1697250, was read next to the decompilation; the floating-point compares were checked with their condition-code operands in a separate disassembly, because the decompilation drops one of them).
  Finds a timing-table format that the board and monitor can start with, and returns its geometry (arguments: screen, an output buffer for the file name, six output words for pixel width, screen height, frame-buffer width, frame-buffer height and the depth-table index, then a last argument handed to the file reader; result 1 when a usable file was found, 10 for an unknown depth, 0 when a needed value is missing). It reads the "/var/X11/Xvc/Odyssey%d_TimingTable" file with `odsyReadTTfilename` (a result of 1 or 3 prints "unable to read or create file" and marks the search as using the default), appends ".vfo" to a name that does not start with '/', and looks the depth the file gave up in the four-entry table at `odsyScrnPriv` + 0x4428, storing the index through the sixth output word; no match prints "%d is not a valid framebuffer depth" and returns 10.
  It then loops over candidate files. A name starting with '/' is used as a path (a trailing newline is cut); otherwise the path is the environment variable `GL_GRROOT`, then "/usr/gfx/ucode/ODSY/vof", a '/' when missing, then the name. If the database does not open, the routine is fatal when it is already on the default ("default timing file '%s' not found") and otherwise prints the errno, asks `odsyValidateBoardConfig` for a board-appropriate default name, appends ".vfo" and repeats. From the database it reads with `SDBgetSymbolValueScalar` (a miss prints "odsyGetScalar: unable to find %s", ends the routine and clears the name buffer, result 0): AchievedFrequency (a double), FormatInfo_Interlaced, FormatInfo_DualHead, FormatInfo_DigitalSkew (the only one whose miss is ignored; it then stays 0), FormatInfo_FullScreenStereo, FormatInfo_Stereo, TotalPixelsPerLine, DCDTotalPixelsPerLine, DCDSupport, DCDHorizontalBackPorch, DCDHorizontalFrontPorch, DCDHorizontalSync (their sum is kept), ActivePixelsPerLine, ActiveLinesPerFrame and FormatInfo_FieldSequential. Stereo is folded into one word: 0 for none, 1 for stereo, 4 when full-screen stereo is also set, plus 2 for field-sequential.
  A format is refused by the rules below. A refusal prints "Illegal timing file '%s' specified" and the default name is substituted before the loop repeats, and is fatal ("Illegal default timing file '%s'") when the default itself was refused. On a board whose record halfword at +0x3a is 3: DCDSupport must be nonzero; AchievedFrequency must lie from 60.0 to 180.0 MHz, or, when the module word at 0x173aa10 (set by platform parameter 0xc) is nonzero, must not exceed 220.0 (no lower limit then); the format must be neither interlaced, nor full-screen stereo, nor field-sequential; and when that word is zero and there is no dual head and no digital skew, the product of 500.0 and the ratio TotalPixelsPerLine over DCDTotalPixelsPerLine, truncated, must not be below the DCD blanking sum. A 1600 by 1024 format is always refused when the first monitor of the board record (valid halfword +0xc6) has the identity bytes 4c f8 41 06 at +0xd0 to +0xd3, and when the second (valid halfword +0x148) has them at +0x152 to +0x155: every outcome of the match tests ends in a refusal, so the rule means "this monitor does not take 1600 by 1024" (what that monitor is, and why, is **unknown**: no software or published source read so far names it). On other boards a dual-head format or one with a digital skew is refused. On any board whose words at +0x28 and +0x18 are 0 and 2, a frequency above 109.0 and below 194.0 is also refused, and so is exactly 108.0 or exactly 107.2512 when the board-private word +0x10 is 3. VfoVersion must be nonzero and FormatInfo_FullScreenStereo must be zero ("Illegal format for X server startup"). On that board type with depth code 0x10 and a name beginning "1280x1024_60" the routine prints that 16 bits a pixel is unsupported with that table (and tells the user to pick new defaults in the toolchest) and sets the depth index to 2.
  On success it reads ActivePixelsPerLine, ScreenHeight, FrameBufferHeight, FrameBufferWidth and FormatInfo_DualHead, rounds the frame-buffer height up to a multiple of 16 and the width up to a multiple of 32, and stores them: with dual head on a halfword-3 board the frame-buffer width is doubled, the pixel width is twice ActivePixelsPerLine and halfword +0x3e of the board record becomes 1, otherwise they are as read and +0x3e becomes 0. The board-information record from `ddxGetBoardInfo` gets the width at +0x20 and the height at +0x22, the screen height goes to the second output, and the routine returns 1 with the database closed. What the halfword at +0x3a of the board record (value 3 for the first rule set) names is **unknown**.

## Gamma ramp routines

The gamma ramp the module keeps for a screen sits behind the video-control record: the word at +0x24 points to a record whose first word is the sample count (0x1000), whose second is 10, and whose word at +0xc points to three tables of 0x600 16-bit entries, red at +0, green at +0xc00 and blue at +0x1800. Entry n of a table stands for a range of the 4096 input samples: entries 0 to 0x1ff are samples 0 to 0x1ff, entries 0x200 to 0x2ff are every second sample from 0x200, and entries 0x300 to 0x5ff are every fourth sample from 0x400 (the compressed index that `odsyLoadGamma0` also walks). The board takes the ramp as 0x600 colour-map entries at index 0x1a00 + n, each the three 16-bit values reduced to 10 bits and packed as red 29:20, green 19:10, blue 9:0.

- `odsyStoreGamma16` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x158f900, 872 bytes): **established.**
  Replaces selected channels of the gamma ramp with a 16-bit ramp and sends the result (arguments: screen, channel mask, unused, sample count, ramp pointer). The mask selects red (bit 0), green (bit 1) and blue (bit 2). The sample count must equal the ramp's first word or "the size of the ramp passed doesn't match the gamma size" is printed and nothing changes. It reserves a 0xf8a0-byte stack block as a colour-load request (count 0x1f00, entries at +0x10; a zero from the reservation prints "couldn't allocate memory"). For each of the 4096 samples the first loop uses the compressed index above, so it visits 0x600 samples: the next ramp value is copied into the selected channels' tables at that index (the stores guarded by mask bits 1, 2 and 4) and an entry (index 0x1a00 plus the table index, packed colour from all three tables) is written. It then fills the byte tables of the video-control record at +0xa8, +0x1a8 and +0x2a8 with an identity run 0 to 0xff (the second loop, whose end test is the constant 0xfe), copies the 0x1900 ordinary colour entries from the board record's shadow table (the pointer at +0x54) into the request, and calls `odsyLoadCmap` and then `odsyGammaFit` with the table pointer.

  The 8-bit form of `odsyStoreGamma16` (same arguments, the ramp is bytes). Each byte b is widened to the 16-bit value b times 0x101 (`CONCAT11` of the byte with itself), so 0xff becomes 0xffff, before it goes into the selected channels' tables; the sample walk, the identity byte tables, the shadow-colour fill, the `odsyLoadCmap` call and the `odsyGammaFit` call are the same, and the failure messages read "odsyStoreGamma8".
- `odsyStoreCompGamma` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x167a3a0, 724 bytes): **established.**
  Sends the stored gamma ramp again without changing it (argument: the screen). Around the `odsyLoadCmap` call it sets the board record's word at +0x13c to 1 and puts the old value back afterwards, so the request is always sent to the kernel (`odsyLoadCmap` sends only when that word is 1); then it calls `odsyGammaFit`. That it exists to re-send the ramp after a compositor change is **inferred** from the forced +0x13c value, which `odsyLoadCmap` tests.
- `odsyInitGammaMap..ED` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1592b80, 1396 bytes): **established.**

Each table entry is `(x ^ (1/gammaAdjustVal)) * 65535 + 0.5` truncated to 16 bits, where x is the sample number divided by 4095 (the module multiplies by 16.003663 and divides by 65535.0) and `gammaAdjustVal` is the module's current fitted value; all three channels get the same value. The loops visit the samples in the three ranges of the compressed index, entries 0 to 0x1ff, 0x200 to 0x2ff and 0x300 to 0x5ff, and each also fills one colour-map entry (index 0x1a00 plus the entry number, with the 10-bit value packed three times). It fills the byte identity tables as `odsyStoreGamma16` does, sends the 0x600 entries with `odsyLoadCmap`, and then stores 292 divided by `gammaAdjustVal`, truncated and limited to 255, in the board-private record at +0x38 and the constant 0x76ff at +0x3c; these are the two operand words of the 0x10845 command that `odsyInitDefaultHW..N` sends.
- `odsyQueryGammaColors` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15ae930, 292 bytes): **established.**
  Reads one channel of the gamma ramp back as 4096 samples (arguments: screen, channel 1, 2 or 3 for red, green or blue, output array of 4096 halfwords). The channel picks the table at +0, +0xc00 or +0x1800 behind the video-control record's pointer chain (+0x24 then +0xc); any other channel number leaves the table pointer unset. The loop that compares against 0x200 and 0x400 (0x15ae9d0 and 0x15ae99c) writes two samples per pass, sample i taking the table entry at the compressed index of i (i itself below 0x200, half of it plus 0x100 below 0x400, a quarter of it plus 0x200 above), so an entry of the 0x600-entry table appears once, twice or four times in the output, by the range it belongs to.
- `odsyGammaFit` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16f6730, 536 bytes): **established.**
  Fits a single exponent to the current ramp and sends the matching display setting (arguments: screen, the pointer to the 16-bit tables). For each of the 0x600 table entries it takes y, the mean of the three channel values (the sum divided by 3 through a multiply by 0xaaaaaaab), and x, the sample the entry stands for (j for entries below 0x200, 2j minus 0x200 up to 0x3ff, 4j minus 0x800 above); entries with y of 0 or x not above 0 are skipped. It accumulates the base-10 logarithms (natural logs times 0.4342945): Sx, Sy, the sum of the products and the sum of the squares of log x, with n the number of entries used, and stores the module's `gammaAdjustVal` as (n Sxx minus Sx squared) over (n Sxy minus Sx Sy), the reciprocal of the least-squares slope of log y against log x. It sends the command word 0x10845 to the display FIFO (through the board-private record's pointer at word 0), then 292.0 divided by `gammaAdjustVal` truncated and limited to 255, then the constant 0x76ff. That the 0x10845 operands set a display-side gain from the fitted exponent is **inferred** from the pairing with `odsyInitGammaMap..ED`, which stores the same two values in the record.

- `odsyAttachXvc` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1605fd0, 4348 bytes): **established** (the whole listing, 0x1605fd0 to 0x16070c8, was read next to the decompilation, with the rodata strings resolved at base 0x172acc0).

It stores in the module word at 0x173aa0c whether the environment variable `XVC_DEBUG` is set, and on the first screen of the process (a flag word at +0x10 of the module's data block) calls `odsyQueryHyperpipeNetwork` once with the screen number and 0. The head count is 1; it is 2 when the board-private record's halfword at +0x3a is 3 and the halfword at +0x3e is 1; and it is 3 when the board record's word at +0x1cc or +0x1d0 is nonzero (0x1606038 to 0x1606060, 0x16065c8). It allocates 0x27bc plus 0x1f8 bytes per head with `Xalloc` and zeroes them (a null allocation returns 0). The head count goes to +4, the head array (entries of 0x1f8 bytes from +0x3ac) to +8, 3 to +0xc, 1 to +0x10, +0x14 and +0x20, -1 to +0x18, and the block after the last head to +0x24 (the one the gamma routines follow). The function table is at +0x34: +0x34 `odsyQryMonitor`, +0x38 `odsyResetProc`, +0x3c `odsyPostInit`, +0x40 `odsyLstVideoFmt`, +0x44 `odsyLoadAndFree`, +0x48 `odsyLstVideoFmtCombs..BC`, +0x4c `odsyListFormatsInComb..IB`, +0x50 `odsyLdCombination..AD`, +0x58 `odsySetCntrl..ID`, +0x5c `odsyQryCntrl..JD`, +0x68 `odsySetScrnGlock`, +0x6c `odsyGenlockHandler..FD`, +0x70 `odsySetPltParam`, +0x74 `odsyQryPltParam`, +0x78 `odsyStoreGamma8`, +0x7c `odsyStoreGamma16`, +0x80 `odsyQueryGammaColors`, +0x8c `odsySetChannelInputRectangle..IC`, +0x90 `odsyQueryBestChannelRectangle..HC`, +0x94 `odsyMonitorCommand..BD`, +0x98 `odsyInitMonitorProtocol..CD`, +0x9c `odsySetExternalLock..GD`, +0xa0 `odsyQryExtSyncNm..HD` and +0xa4 `odsyLdFmtByName..OC`. The first head gets the screen's height and width as floats at +0x3b8 and +0x3bc, and the 0x138-byte format-name area at +0x3c0 is zeroed.
  The format file is opened as a path when its name starts with '/' (a newline is cut off), otherwise `odsyMakeFileName` builds it under "/usr/gfx/ucode/ODSY/vof"; `SDBreadOpenDatabase` failing prints "failed to open %s sdb file ... specified in /var/X11/Xvc/Odyssey%d_TimingTable file ... using default monitor settings instead" (the %d is a byte of the board record behind the screen's slot) and takes the common failure exit. From the database it reads, each with `SDBgetSymbolValueScalar` and, on a miss, "odsyGetScalar: unable to find %s" and the failure exit: FieldsPerFrame (+0x4ec), FormatInfo_Interlaced, FormatInfo_Stereo, FormatInfo_FullScreenStereo and FormatInfo_FieldSequential (locals), VerticalRetraceRate (a double: the float at +0x4d4 is the rate, the float at +0x4d0 is the rate times FieldsPerFrame when the format is not interlaced and the rate itself when it is), and ScreenHeight (+0x4c0), ActivePixelsPerLine (+0x4c4), TotalLinesPerFrame (+0x4c8), TotalPixelsPerLine (+0x4cc), FormatInfo_PixelClock (+0x4d8), FormatInfo_H_BackPorch (+0x4dc), FormatInfo_H_Sync (+0x4e0), FormatInfo_H_FrontPorch (+0x4e4) and FormatInfo_H_Active (+0x4e8). The stereo word at +0x4f4 is 0 without stereo, 1 with stereo, 4 with stereo and full-screen stereo, plus 2 for a field-sequential format.
  With FieldsPerFrame at zero the field-array pointer at +0x4f0 is cleared. Otherwise it `calloc`s FieldsPerFrame records of 0x24 bytes ("odsyAttachXvc: Field info alloc failed!") and four word arrays (the first failure prints "Couldn't allocate FieldOffset", the other three "Couldn't allocate FieldSkip", each freeing the arrays made before), reads FieldLineOffset, FieldLineSkip, FieldColor and FieldEye into them with `SDBgetSymbolValueArray`, and for each field copies FieldLineOffset to the record's +0 and FieldLineSkip to +4, FieldColor to +0x1c and FieldEye to +0x20. For +8 to +0x18 of every record it reads the five names FormatInfo_F_0_V_BackPorch, _V_Sync, _V_SyncPulse, _V_FrontPorch and _V_Active (the field-0 names, read again for each record so all records get the same values); on a board whose halfword +0x3e is 1 it instead reads TotalPixelsPerLine and DCDTotalPixelsPerLine and stores for each name DCDTotalPixelsPerLine times the truncated quotient of the value over TotalPixelsPerLine (the sync-pulse value goes to both +0xc and +0x10). The four word arrays are then freed. Next the format name without its last four characters (the file suffix) is copied to +0x3c0, a block of per-format words from +0x558 to +0x5a0 and +0x4fc to +0x504 is cleared or set to 1 or -1 (+0x554 and +0x500 are 1, +0x598 is -1), and `odsyLoadTimingTable..CC` is called with (screen, database, name area, 0, -1) ("odsyAttachXvc: odsyLoadTimingTable Failed"), then `odsyInitGammaMap..ED` ("cannot initialize the gamma map.").

The last head entry takes the compositor words: the board word +0x1cc goes to entry offset +0x1e8, and when +0x1d0 is nonzero the entry's words are cleared (+0x1e0 and +0x154 set to 1) and +0x1d0 replaces the +0x1e8 word. It sets `screenIsSaved` to 1, calls `XSGIvcScreenInit` with the screen and the record and returns 1. The database is closed on every path. On a failure after the allocation it frees the field-record array of each head and returns 0 without freeing the record itself (the listing at 0x1606518 to 0x1606584 shows no free of it).
- `odsyPostInit` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15675e0, 1848 bytes): **established** (the whole listing, 0x15675e0 to 0x1567d14, was read next to the decompilation).

It returns at once, touching nothing, when the monitor-information table pointer `moninfoData` is null (the compare at 0x156763c). Otherwise it first looks, with `strcasecmp`, for a record whose name equals the name at the start of the video-control record, walking `numMonitors` records of 0x4c bytes (loop 0x156767c to 0x15676a4).
  With a match it takes the record's pair list (count at +0x44, pointer at +0x48, 12 bytes a pair: kind word, value word). Pass one copies the value of every kind-6 pair into a 50-word local array; a 51st prints "odsyPostInit: stepping over array boundary!" through `ErrorF` and stops collecting (0x15677c8 to 0x1567830). Pass two, run only when at least one kind-6 value was found, takes each kind-7 pair's value as a candidate width and each kind-6 value as a candidate height (millimetres, as the factor-of-ten paths below show), forms the float ratio candidate-width over candidate-height, subtracts the screen's pixel aspect ratio (`screen +8` over `+0xa`, both signed halfwords, converted to float) and keeps the pair with the smallest absolute difference; the best starts at the float constant 100.0 and an equal difference does not displace an earlier pair. The screen's own halfwords at +0xc and +0xe are the starting width and height, so they stay when no pair is scanned. The winner is stored as width (+0xc, the kind-7 value) and height (+0xe, the kind-6 value) at 0x1567b58, and when the video-control record's word at +4 is 2 the width is doubled (0x1567b64 to 0x1567ba8). This path ends there; the aspect cut below is not applied to it.
  With no matching record it reads the board-private record's pointer at +0x5c. When that record's halfword at +0x3a is not 3 it returns without a change if the halfword at +0x44 is zero, and otherwise sets the width to the byte at +0x5b times 10 and the height to the byte at +0x5c times 10. When the halfword is 3 the record holds one monitor identity block per head, with a valid halfword at +0xc6 (first head) or +0x148 (second head), a width byte at +0xdd or +0x15f and a height byte at +0xde or +0x160. Neither valid returns unchanged. Both valid: the height is the smaller of the two height bytes times 10, and the width is the smaller width byte times 10, or the sum of the two width bytes times 10 when the halfword at +0x3e of the same record is nonzero. Exactly one valid: the height is that head's height byte times 10 and the width is its width byte times 10, or times 20 when the +0x3e halfword is nonzero. All of these paths then reach the final step, which shrinks the width to the height times the pixel aspect ratio (float, truncated) when the width is larger than that (0x1567704 to 0x156775c). That the identity bytes and the table values are physical sizes in centimetres and millimetres is **inferred** from the factor of 10 and the name of the screen fields; the +0x3e halfword being a "heads side by side" flag is **inferred** from its only effect, widening the width.

## Colour-map update routines

- `odsyStoreColors` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16e5800, 1096 bytes): **established.**
  Sends changed colour-map cells of one X colormap to the board (arguments: colormap, number of entries, array of 12-byte X colour items). The visual behind the colormap (first word) has its class in the halfword at +4; a TrueColor visual (class 4) returns at once, as does a colormap with no board slot (its private index word is negative). The colormap's base cell comes from the screen's table at +0x74 of the structure behind the screen's +0x74 (28 bytes an entry, the word at +0x18), indexed by that private word. For a DirectColor visual (class 5) each item names its cells through the visual's three masks and shifts (words +0xc, +0x10 and +0x14 with shifts at +0x18, +0x1c and +0x20): for every component flagged in the item's byte at +10 (bit 0 red, bit 1 green, bit 2 blue) the cell is the base plus the masked and shifted pixel, and the new word keeps the other two 10-bit components from the shadow table (the pointer at +0x54 of the board-private record) and takes the flagged component from the item's 16-bit value masked to 0xffc0 and moved into place. For every other class the cell is the base plus the item's pixel and the word is red in bits 29:20 (the 16-bit value masked to 0xffc0, shifted left 14), green in 19:10 (masked, shifted left 4) and blue in 9:0 (the value shifted right 6); the loop handles two items a pass. The entries are written after a 0x10-byte header in a stack block sized from the item count (a zero from the reservation prints "couldn't allocate memory") and `odsyLoadCmap` receives the block with the count in its first halfword.
- `odsyInstallColormap` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x168c4f0, 916 bytes): **established.**
  Loads a whole colormap into the board when it becomes the installed one (argument: the colormap; no result). A TrueColor visual (class 4) returns at once. The base cell is found as in `odsyStoreColors`. For a DirectColor visual every one of the visual's cells (count at visual +8) gets an entry whose word packs the red, green and blue values of the three per-channel entry arrays (the colormap's words at +0x38, +0x3c and +0x40, 0x14 bytes an entry) as red 29:20, green 19:10, blue 9:0, each masked to 0xffc0 and shifted. For the other classes only cells that are in use are sent: a static visual (class bit 0 clear) sends every cell, a dynamic one only cells whose reference-count halfword at entry +0xc is nonzero and, when the colormap has an allocation bit mask, whose bit in that mask is set; a shared cell's three values are read through the pointers in the entry. The number of entries that went into the block is stored in its first halfword and `odsyLoadCmap` is called once, nothing being sent when no cell qualified.
- `odsyChangeDIDCmap` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1632890, 948 bytes): **established** (the whole listing, 0x1632890 to 0x1632c40, was read next to the decompilation).

The window's resource-manager private is the slot `rrmWindowPrivateIndex` of the window's private array (window +0x84); the screen's resource-manager record is the slot `rrmScreenPrivateIndex` of the screen's (+0x1b4). It returns without a change when the private's identifier word at +0x14 is negative, the colormap is null or the colormap's slot number (the word behind the colormap's +0x44) is negative (0x16328f0 to 0x1632908).
  The colormap's cell page is the word at +0x18 of that slot's 28-byte entry in the table behind the screen record's +0x74 (its own +0x74), shifted right 8 (arithmetic). The window's display-mode word at +0x24 of the private holds the page in a bit field that depends on the identifier: below 0x20 the field is bits 8:4 (mask 0x1f0, page shifted left 4), from 0x20 up it is bits 7:3 (mask 0xf8, page shifted left 3). The per-identifier entry is 0x24 bytes at `rrm record + id*0x24`, with a doubly linked window list (head +0x98, tail +0x9c), a flag halfword at +0xa8 and a use count at +0xac. When the entry's flag bit 0 is clear, or the page already in the +0x24 word equals the new one, the routine skips the re-assignment: the +0x24 word and the identifier stay as they are and the mode word sent is the stored word with the field replaced by the new page.
