A negative result prints "odsyChangeDIDCmap: Can't load display mode" and then "rnid=0x%x, clipid=0x%x, errno='%s'" with the first two block words and `strerror(errno)`. Last it stores the identifier, the flag word and the mode word in the board-private record's table behind +0x58, 12 bytes an identifier (0x1632b10 to 0x1632b48). That bit 30 selects the overlay or underlay sense of the mode word is **inferred** from its dependence on the private's two flag bits only.

## Cursor record routines

- `odsyRealizeCursor` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1582940, 1212 bytes): **established.**
  Builds the module's per-screen cursor record for an X cursor (arguments: screen, cursor; result 1, or 0 after a failed allocation). It allocates a 16-byte record with `Xalloc` and stores it in the cursor's word at index screen number + 5 ("odsyRealizeCursor: memory allocation failed" on failure), allocates the 0x300-byte glyph and alpha buffer (the pointer goes to +8; a failure frees the record, prints "nfbRealizeCursor: memory allocation failed" and returns 0), zeroes the buffer, and sets the record's word at +0 and +4 to 0 and the halfword at +0xc to 1. Width and height come from the cursor bits' halfwords at +8 and +10, each limited to 32. For every row it fills 16 bytes of glyph (four 32-bit words at the row's offset in the first 512 bytes) and 8 bytes of alpha (two words at +0x200 in the buffer): the row's mask word, cut by a left-aligned width mask, is expanded to two bits a pixel with value 3 where the mask bit is set (the 16-iteration loop that shifts 0x8000 right), and the source word ANDed with that masked word goes through the 16-word nibble table at rodata offset 0xb70 (the table in `odsyDisplayCursor`) for the glyph words, which hold 1 where a source-and-mask bit is set. This is the same fill as the table path of `odsyDisplayCursor`; because the record's second-colour pointer at +4 stays 0, the other path of that routine never applies to a cursor made here.
- `nfbUnrealizeCursor` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x168ae50, 208 bytes): **established.**
  Releases a cursor's record for a screen (arguments: screen, cursor; result 1). The record is the cursor's word at index screen number + 5; if there is none the routine returns 1 at once (0x168aef4). The glyph buffer at +8 is freed with `Xfree`; when that pointer is null the message "WSGO! Unrealize nocache cursor with no data!" is printed instead. The object at +4 is freed when present, the record is freed, the slot in the cursor is cleared and 1 is returned.
- `nfbCursorLimits` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16b8160, 84 bytes): **established.**
  Clips a cursor's box to the screen (arguments: screen, unused, input box of four 16-bit values x1, y1, x2, y2, output box). x1 and y1 are limited below by 0, x2 is limited above by the screen's width halfword at +8 and y2 by its height halfword at +10; the output box holds the four results and nothing else is touched.
- `nfbRecolorCursor` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x162d0f0, 56 bytes): **established.**
  Forwards a cursor recolour request (arguments: screen, a second argument it does not read, cursor). When the cursor is null it returns without doing anything (the branch at 0x162d104); otherwise it calls the procedure stored at +0x11c of the screen with its arguments unchanged (the `jalr` at 0x162d110 after `lw t9,0x11c(a0)`).

## Screen initialisation

- `odsyInit` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x156f890, 5208 bytes): **established** (the whole listing, 0x156f890 to 0x1570ce4, was read next to the decompilation; the earlier reading was corrected where noted).
  The module's screen initialiser (arguments include the screen at the second position; result 1, or 0 after any failure, each of which frees what was allocated). On the first screen of a server generation it allocates the module's screen and graphics-context private indexes (`odsyScreenPrivateIndex`, `odsyGCPrivateIndex`), then an 8-byte graphics-context private and a 0x140-byte board-private record that it zeroes, sets the word at +0x13c to 1 (the cmap-send enable `odsyLoadCmap` tests) clears the words at +0x74, +0x78 and +0x88 and points +0x5c at the board-information record from `ddxGetBoardInfo` (called with the byte at +0xc of the screen's board structure) plus 0x28. If the generation check fails because an index allocation returns a negative number, or the 0x140-byte allocation fails, the routine returns 0 at once. It calls `odsyDefaultTTExists` with the six output slots in its stack frame for the starting format ("No default timing table and framebuffer config!!!!" when none is found), stores the returned sizes, depth code and index (record +0x10, +0x14, +0x18, +0x1c, and the width in 16-pixel units at +0xc), and calls `odsyKernInit..O` to start the kernel side (a result other than 1 returns 0). From the board's display-record bytes at +0xc, +0xe, +0xf and +8 and +0xa it sets the default visual class, depth, id and overlay choice (+0x2c to +0x38), taking the server defaults `ddxDfltClass`, `ddxDfltDepth` and `ddxDfltVisualID` when a byte is 0xff or 0, and 1 for the overlay when `ddxOverlayFlag` is set. It allocates 23 hardware colour-map groups with `nfbInitHWCmapArrays`; the depth index indexes a rodata word table at 0x680 that gives the visual-mask bit to test (entries 0, 0, 1 and 2 for indexes 0 to 3, so indexes 0 and 1 print "odsyInit: unsupported FBdepth index: %d" and fail), and two loops count the entries of the module's capability table (`odsyCapabilityInfo`) that suit the board (the board record's word at +0x50 and +0x34 and the mask bits tested against 0x30 and 0x100) to size the arrays it allocates next (0x24, 0x14 and 0x44 bytes an entry, two 0x2640-byte colour tables and four word tables for the shadow and valid-region data: "failed to alloc shadow colormap", "failed to alloc validRegions"). It then runs `nfbGenericScreenInit` ("nfbGenericScreenInit failed"), allocates the screen-private index of the zero-width line code once per generation, runs `nfbHWColormapScreenInit` with the colour-map group arrays, allocates a 0x8000-byte shadow colour table stored at +0x54 of the board record ("failed to alloc shadow colormap", which also frees the group arrays), reads the display register information with `ReadDisplayRegisterInfo`, and runs `odsyAttachXvc` with the starting format name, `odsyBlackCmap`, `rrmInit` (the board-private word +0x68 first receives the descriptor from `odsyKernInit..O`) and `odsyInitDefaultHW..N`. Each failure from `nfbHWColormapScreenInit` on frees the board record and the group arrays and returns 0. It then makes the client id for the default colormap with `FakeClientID(0)` and creates the colormap with `rrmCreateDefColormap`, clears the module's per-region cache table, and, the first time only, reads the machine's inventory with `scaninvent` through `odsyScanAudioInventory..K` (a negative result prints "scaninvent can't read inventory table" and returns 0); when the inventory word is 0 it installs `odsyBell` and `odsyKeyClick` in the screen's procedures at +0xc and +0x10, otherwise it sets the word to 1. It then runs `glxScreenInit` with `odsyglxScreenPriv`, allocates the 0x18-byte block stored at +0x40 of the board record and initialises two regions in it with the screen's region procedure at +0x154, and finally reads these environment variables, each applied with `atoi` when set and nonempty and stored in a module word: `ODSY_DMA_THRESHOLD` (0x17345e0) and `ODSY_PIO_THRESHOLD` (0x17345e4), the thresholds of `odsyDrawImageSingleBuffer..J`, `ODSY_REPLICATE_TILE_THRESHOLD` (0x17345d8), `ODSY_REPLICATE_TILE_FOR_CP_THRESHOLD` (0x17345dc) and `ODSY_COPY_WINDOW_WAR` (0x1738220). `ODSY_RECT_SPAN_WIDTH_THRESHOLD` is looked up and converted with `atoi`, but no store follows the call at 0x1570910, so its value is discarded and setting it has no effect. What the four stored thresholds other than the first two control is not read in this routine. The failure messages seen in the listing are "odsyInit: No default timing table and framebuffer config!!!!", "unsupported FBdepth index", "nfbGenericScreenInit failed", "failed to alloc shadow colormap", "failed to alloc validRegions" and "scaninvent can't read inventory table".

## Window display-identifier routines

The resource-manager client keeps one record per screen (the screen-private slot `rrmScreenPrivateIndex`) and one record per window (the window-private slot `rrmWindowPrivateIndex`). The routines below all use the same fields, read from their listings. Screen record: the number of display identifiers at +0, a mask for the window's first mode word at +0x10 and for its second at +0x14, the flag word at +0xc (bit 0 is tested by `FindFreeID`), the word at +0x30 (nonzero allows reserved entries to be reclaimed), procedures at +0x20 (called with a window, 8 and 1 to evict it) and +0x48 (called with a window and its previous identifier after an assignment), and an array of 0x24-byte identifier entries from +0x98: the head and tail of the entry's window list (+0x98, +0x9c), two mode words (+0xa0, +0xa4), a flag halfword (+0xa8), the entry's window class (halfword +0xaa) and the number of windows on it (+0xac). Window record: a flag halfword at +0 whose bit 3 means "on an identifier list", the window class (halfword +2), the identifier (word +0x14, -1 for none), two mode words (+0x20, +0x24) and the list links (+0x2c previous, +0x30 next). The entry flag bits are used as follows: bit 0 marks a reserved entry (`FindFreeID` tests it, and unlinking turns a reserved entry's bits 1 and 2 on); bit 1 is set by an assignment and means in use; bit 2 means shared (set by a second assignment, and by an unlink while head and tail differ); bit 4 is cleared by an unlink that empties the list; bit 5 is kept through an unlink and blocks the reclaim in `FindFreeID`. These meanings are **inferred** from the code that sets and tests the bits. Every routine below unlinks a window with the same sequence: the previous window's next link (or the entry head) takes the window's next, the next window's previous link (or the entry tail) takes the window's previous, both links are cleared, the entry's count is lowered, the entry flags become the old bits 0, 4 and 5 plus bits 1 and 2 when bit 0 was set, then bit 4 cleared when the list is empty or bit 1 (head equals tail) or bits 1 and 2 (they differ) set, and the window's list flag is cleared.

- `AssignID..FG` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15e96a0, 308 bytes): **established** (whole listing 0x15e96a0 to 0x15e97d0).
  Puts a window on a display identifier's list (arguments: window, identifier; no result of its own, it ends by calling a screen procedure). It stores the identifier in the window record's +0x14 and in the word at +4 of the window's frame-buffer private (slot `nfbWindowPrivateIndex`), remembering the old value of that word, clears the window's next link, sets its previous link to the entry's tail and appends it (the entry head when the list was empty, otherwise the old tail's next link), sets the window's list flag, counts the window in the entry (+0xac) and ORs 2 into the entry flags. When the count was 0 before (the first window) and the entry's bit 0 is clear it calls `SetDIDMode` for the window first; when the count becomes 2 or more it ORs 6 into the flags. It finally jumps to the screen record's procedure at +0x48 with the window and the old frame-buffer word (a tail call at 0x15e9784 and 0x15e97a8).
- `NewID..GG` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x162eb60, 296 bytes): **established** (whole listing 0x162eb60 to 0x162ec84).
  Moves a window to a different display identifier (arguments: window, new identifier; the second argument is passed through untouched to the next routine). When the window already has an identifier (word +0x14 not negative) and is on a list, it unlinks the window from its present entry with the sequence above; it then sets the window's identifier word to -1 and tail-calls `AssignID..FG` with the window and the new identifier (0x162ec58). A window with no identifier goes straight to `AssignID..FG` (0x162ec60).
- `cmapDID` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1636ba0, 336 bytes): **established** (whole listing 0x1636ba0 to 0x1636cec).
  Returns the display identifier that goes with a window's colormap (argument: window; result the identifier). The window's record at +0x78 (made by a helper called with the window when it is null, 0x1636bd0) gives a colormap id at +8; a window whose class byte (+1) is 2 uses id 0. `LookupIDByType(id, 6)` finds the colormap; when it exists and its first slot word (behind +0x44) is not negative, the result is word +0x10 of that slot's 28-byte entry in the table behind the screen record's +0x74. Otherwise the record's first word (a visual number) minus the base in the screen structure's +0x50 indexes the table at +0x58 (0x14 bytes an entry), and the result is that entry's first word. That +0x78 names a visual record, and the +0x58 table is per visual, is **inferred** from the arithmetic.
- `FindBestID` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x157e810, 656 bytes): **established** (whole listing 0x157e810 to 0x157ea9c).
  Chooses the display identifier for a window whose class or colormap may have changed (argument: window; no result). It scans all identifiers: an entry matches when its class halfword equals the window's class and, under the masks at +0x10 and +0x14 of the screen record, the window's two mode words equal the entry's two. The last matching entry is the candidate, except that a matching entry with flag bit 2 set is taken at once: if the window already has that identifier the routine returns, otherwise the window is unlinked, its identifier word set to -1 and `AssignID..FG` is called with that entry (0x157e980 to 0x157ea50). With a candidate that has no bit 2, every window on the candidate's list is evicted by calling the screen procedure at +0x20 with (window, 0, 1) (the loop at 0x157e920, which follows each window's next link), then `NewID..GG` moves this window to the candidate. With no match it takes the identifier from `cmapDID` and calls `NewID..GG` unless the window already has it (0x157ea5c to 0x157ea7c).
- `FindFreeID` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x171e8c0, 920 bytes): **established** (whole listing 0x171e8c0 to 0x171ec54).
  Gives a window a display identifier no other window uses (argument: window; result 1 when it has one, 0 when none could be found). A class-1 window on a screen whose flag word has bit 0 set takes the identifier equal to the identifier count (the entry past the table) and returns 1 (0x171ebf8). A window that already has an identifier whose entry has flag bit 2 clear keeps it and returns 1. Otherwise the first entry of the window's class that has flag bit 0 clear and no windows on it takes the window (after an unlink from the old entry and the identifier word set to -1, `AssignID..FG` is called, result 1). If none exists and the screen record's word +0x30 is nonzero, a second scan finds an entry of the class with bit 0 set (reserved), bits 5 and 1 clear and no windows, zeroes that entry's flag halfword and assigns the window to it (result 1); otherwise the result is 0.
- `SetReservedID` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1719690, 1612 bytes): **established** (whole listing 0x1719690 to 0x1719cd8).
  Turns a display identifier into a reserved one and re-homes the windows that were on it (arguments: screen, identifier; no result). It first takes every window off the entry's list: the loop at 0x171976c saves the list head in a stack array, calls the screen record's procedure at +0x20 with (window, 0, 0) when the window record's flag byte at +6 has bit 3 set (halfword bit 11), unlinks it from its present entry with the common sequence and sets its identifier word to -1. Then the entry's two mode words (+0xa0, +0xa4) are replaced by the words at +0xb0 and +0xb4 of the same entry, the screen record's procedure at +0x2c is called with (screen, identifier) (its job is **unknown**: it is called through a table slot the module does not name here), and the entry's flags get bit 1 set. Each saved window is then given a new identifier by what is `FindFreeID`'s logic written inline: a class-1 window on a screen whose flag word has bit 0 set takes the identifier equal to the identifier count; a window that has no identifier, or whose entry has flag bit 2, takes the first entry of its class with bit 0 clear and no windows (`AssignID..FG`), or else a reserved unused entry that it clears (only when the record's word +0x30 is nonzero), or else `StealID` (0x17198e4 and 0x1719af0). If the entry's old flags had bit 4 set (0x10) that bit is ORed into the flags of the window's new entry and the procedure at +0x20 is called with (window, 8, 1) (0x17198ec to 0x1719930).
- `FindFreeCID` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15b8810, 2628 bytes): **established** (whole listing 0x15b8810 to 0x15b9244 and its tail blocks; the three assignment blocks differ only in which entry they use).
  Gives a window a clip identifier, the analogue of `FindFreeID` for the screen record's second table (argument: window; no result). The clip-identifier table is at +0x94 of the screen record (0x1c-byte entries: list head, list tail, flag halfword at +8, class halfword at +0xa, window count at +0xc), the count is at +4 and a round-robin cursor at +0x88; the window record keeps its clip identifier at +0x18, its list links at +0x3c (previous) and +0x40 (next) and its on-list flag as bit 6 (0x40) of its first halfword. A screen procedure at +0x5c is called with the window; when it returns 0 the window takes the identifier equal to the count (word at +4) and the routine returns (0x15b886c, 0x15b904c). Otherwise a window that already has an identifier whose entry has flag bit 2 clear keeps it. Else it scans the entries other than the window's own for one of the window's class (or, for a class-1 window, any entry when the screen flag word has bit 1 set) with flag bit 0 clear: the first one with no windows is taken at once (the old entry is left by the unlink, which keeps bit 0, adds 4 for a reserved entry, sets 2 when the list is not empty and 4 when its head and tail differ), the window is appended to the entry's list, its on-list flag is set, the count is raised and 2 ORed into the flags (6 when the count reaches 2). An entry in use is remembered as a victim when the byte 4 bytes into its head window's record (`lbu` at 0x15b892c) differs from the byte 6 bytes into it (`lbu` at 0x15b8930). Without a free entry, the last victim (or, with no victim, the entry that the round-robin cursor reaches after it is incremented and wrapped to 1 when it passes the count) is cleared: its head window gets the screen procedure at +0x20 with (window, 2, 0), is unlinked and put on entry 0's list with clip identifier 0, and the requesting window is unlinked from its own entry and appended to the victim's (0x15b8958 to 0x15b9244). That the head-window bytes at +4 and +6 are a pending-versus-current state is **inferred**.

## Empty and constant-result routines of the shared X code

Each of these is a whole routine of two instructions, `jr ra` and the delay slot, read in full; none touches memory except where it says so.

- `ZBuffer..LF` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x158f300, 8 bytes): **established.**
  A void routine that does nothing: `jr ra` at 0x158f300 and a no-op at 0x158f304, so its arguments are never read and no result register is set.
- `nfb5RopLoop..FH` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16562e0, 8 bytes): **established.**
  Another empty body, the return at 0x16562e0 with a no-op after it; this is the placeholder behind the five-operand raster-op loop slot of the frame-buffer layer, and it leaves every register as it found it.
- `nfb5MaskRopLoop..FI` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1718210, 8 bytes): **established.**
  The masked sibling of the previous routine is just as empty: `jr ra` at 0x1718210, no-op at 0x1718214, nothing read or written.
- `miChangeGC` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15fd090, 8 bytes): **established.**
  The machine-independent graphics-context change hook is a bare return at 0x15fd090 (no-op delay slot): a change to the context's fields is not acted on by this routine.
- `miCopyGC` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16c0410, 8 bytes): **established.**
  The context-copy hook likewise only returns (0x16c0410, no-op at 0x16c0414), so copying one context to another has no side effect here.
- `nfbChangeGC..LJ` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1620dc0, 8 bytes): **established.**
  The frame-buffer layer's context-change entry is an immediate return at 0x1620dc0 and does nothing with the context it is given.
- `nfbCopyGC..BK` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1669fb0, 8 bytes): **established.**
  The frame-buffer layer's context-copy entry is also an immediate return (0x1669fb0, no-op delay slot).
- `mfbUnrealizeFont` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15bfe30, 8 bytes): **established.**
  Reports success without touching the font: `jr ra` at 0x15bfe30 with `li v0,1` in the delay slot at 0x15bfe34.
- `mfbRealizeFont` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x162ca40, 8 bytes): **established.**
  Also answers 1 and nothing else (`li v0,1` at 0x162ca44 behind the return at 0x162ca40); the monochrome layer keeps no realised-font data here.
- `nfbPositionWindow` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16afbc0, 8 bytes): **established.**
  Window repositioning always succeeds without work: the result is the constant 1 loaded at 0x16afbc4, and neither the window nor the screen is read.
- `nfbUnrealizeWindow` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16fd920, 8 bytes): **established.**
  The unmap hook returns 1 (0x16fd924) and does nothing else.
- `nfbNoopDDACreateScreenResources` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16f5ea0, 8 bytes): **established.**
  The device-dependent screen-resource creation step of the frame-buffer layer is a stub that returns 1 (`li v0,1` at 0x16f5ea4), so no resources are allocated through this slot.
- `nfbNoopDDATranslateBackingStore` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x160d120, 8 bytes): **established.**
  Returns 0 (the delay slot at 0x160d124 is `or v0,zero,zero`) and reads nothing: no backing-store translation is offered.
- `nfbNoopDDAClearBackingStore` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x171dbd0, 8 bytes): **established.**
  Returns 0 (0x171dbd4) with no other action, the same shape as the translate stub above.
- `miRegionExtents` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15e5ab0, 8 bytes): **established.**
  Hands back its first argument unchanged (`or v0,a0,zero` at 0x15e5ab4); that is the address of the bounding box because the box is the first member of a region record.
- `miGetLayerWindow` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16e39f0, 8 bytes): **established.**
  Returns the word at +0x24 of the window record (`lw v0,0x24(a0)` at 0x16e39f4), which is the window's parent pointer in the X server's `WindowRec`, so the layer window of a window is its parent here.

## Forwarding routines (audio library, format-file finders, symbol-database calls)

The audio-library and symbol-database routines are statically linked library code inside the module (`libaudio` and a symbol-table package); the entries give what the code at the address does. Where a routine forwards, its arguments reach the target unchanged unless the entry says otherwise; the target is a static routine without a dynamic symbol, named by address.

- `ALnewconfig` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1550410, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Old-style audio-library name for creating a configuration object; the body builds `gp`, then `bgezall` at 0x155042c transfers to `alNewConfig` at 0x1551960 with the argument registers untouched and returns its result.
- `ALfreeconfig` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1550450, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Forwards to `alFreeConfig` at 0x1551a10 through the same `bgezall` jump (0x155046c); no argument is changed.
- `ALsetconfig` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1550490, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Jumps (0x15504ac) to `alSetConfig` at 0x1552450 with its two arguments as received.
- `ALgetconfig` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15504d0, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Jumps (0x15504ec) to `alGetConfig` at 0x1552740 and returns what it returns.
- `ALsetwidth` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1550510, 52 bytes): **established.**
  A real call rather than a jump: `jalr` at 0x155052c to `alSetWidth` (0x1561cb0) from a frame that saves `gp` and `ra`, then returns the callee's result.
- `ALgetwidth` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1550550, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Calls `alGetWidth` at 0x15624c0 (`jalr` at 0x155056c) and passes the result back.
- `ALsetfloatmax` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1550690, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Calls `alSetFloatMax` at 0x1562320 (`jalr` at 0x15506ac) and returns its result; the argument is a floating-point maximum, passed through in the argument registers.
- `ALopenport` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1550750, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Jumps (0x155076c) to `alOpenPort` at 0x1552e80 with the port name, direction and configuration it was given.
- `ALgetfd` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1550790, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Jumps (0x15507ac) to `alGetFD` at 0x1552290, which yields the port's file descriptor.
- `ALseterrorhandler` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15516a0, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Jumps (0x15516bc) to `alSetErrorHandler` at 0x15518e0, the routine below that installs the handler.
- `alSetErrorHandler` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15518e0, 64 bytes): **established.**
  Replaces the library's error-handler pointer, a global word (0x1742360). It loads the old pointer and compares it with the library's built-in default at 0x1551860; if the old value is that default, the value returned is 1 instead of the pointer. The new value is stored unless the argument is 1, in which case the default is put back. So 1 stands for "default handler" in both directions.
- `alGetErrorString` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1551920, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Maps an error number to its text: for a number from 0 to 26 (the signed compares at 0x1551920 and 0x1551934) it returns the pointer stored at that index of the 27-entry table at 0x1732558; any other number returns 0.
- `ALgetfilled` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1550250, 76 bytes): **established.**
  Number of samples waiting in a port's ring buffer. It reads two pointers from the port record (+0x10 and +0x14), takes the difference of the words they point to, adds the ring size at +8 when that is negative, then scales by shifting right by the word at +0x80 and left by the word at +0x7c (bytes to sample units).
- `ALgetfillable` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15501f0, 84 bytes): **established.**
  The free space in the same ring: it takes the word behind the +0x10 pointer minus the word behind the +0x14 pointer (the opposite order to `ALgetfilled`), subtracts a reserve held at +0x58, wrapped by the ring size at +8 when negative and scaled by the same two shift words at +0x80 and +0x7c.
- `alGetParams` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1562af0, 60 bytes): **established.**
  Calls the shared parameter reader `__alParams` at 0x1562560 with three constants added after the caller's arguments: 1 in the fourth register and -1 and 1 in the fifth and sixth; it is the "get" flavour of that reader.
- `_AL2WriteNToN_ADAT` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15559c0, 60 bytes): **established.**
  Copies sample frames between buffers unchanged: `bcopy` (0x15559e4) with the byte count equal to the frame count shifted left by the converter record's word at +0x80 plus 2 (four bytes a channel scaled by the record's shift).
- `_AL2WriteNToN_AES` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1555970, 72 bytes): **established.**
  Same straight copy for the 3-byte-per-sample AES format: the byte count is frames times three (`sll`+`addu` forms 3n at 0x155598c to 0x155599c), shifted by the record's word at +0x80 plus 2, then `bcopy`.
- `_AL2WriteNToN_AESv` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15599e0, 60 bytes): **established.**
  Triples the fourth argument (`sll`/`addu` at 0x15599f8 to 0x1559a04) and jumps to `_AL2WriteNToN_24v` at 0x1559a20: the voiced AES writer is the 24-bit one with the channel count scaled to bytes.
- `_AL2ReadNFromN_ADAT` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1556f00, 72 bytes): **established.**
  The reverse copy: swaps the first two arguments (0x1556f18 to 0x1556f24) so source and destination trade places, then `bcopy`s frames shifted left by the record's +0x80 plus 2.
- `_AL2ReadNFromN_AES` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1556ea0, 84 bytes): **established.**
  The 3-byte-sample reader, the mirror of `_AL2WriteNToN_AES`: the source and destination arguments are swapped into the `bcopy` call (0x1556eb4, 0x1556ec0, 0x1556ecc) and the byte count is three times the frame count, shifted left by the converter record's word at +0x80 plus 2.
- `_AL2ReadNFromN_AESv` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x155d2c0, 60 bytes): **established.**
  Multiplies the fourth argument by three (0x155d2d8 to 0x155d2e4) and jumps to `_AL2ReadNFromN_24v` at 0x155d300; the voiced AES reader is the 24-bit reader with a byte-sized stride.
- `_AL2Read4ChanFromStereo_16` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1558cc0, 84 bytes): **established.**
  Expands a stereo stream of 32-bit words into four-channel 16-bit frames. For each of the count (third argument) input pairs it stores the left word shifted right by 8 at +0 of the output frame, the right word shifted right by 8 at +2, and zero at +4 and +6 (the loop at 0x1558ce0 to 0x1558d08); the output advances by 8 bytes a frame.
- `_AL2Read4ChanFromStereo_8` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1558d20, 84 bytes): **established.**
  The 8-bit form of the same expansion: input words shifted right by 16 become bytes 0 and 1 of a 4-byte output frame, bytes 2 and 3 are zero (loop 0x1558d40 to 0x1558d68).
- `_AL2recalcscalefactors` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1552e30, 80 bytes): **established.**
  Recomputes six cached conversion factors from the sample rate stored as a double at +0x48 of the converter record. With r the rate: doubles at +0x98 and +0xa0 get r times 2^-23 and r times 2^-24 (the constants 1.1920929e-07 and 5.9604645e-08 at 0x173f740 and 0x173f748), the double at +0xa8 gets 2^23 divided by r (8388608.0), and floats at +0x88, +0x8c and +0x90 hold the narrowed copies of the same three.
- `nfbInfPolyText8..CL` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16cd920, 76 bytes): **established.**
  Dispatches the 8-bit text request to the context's own operation table. The context (second argument) holds its device-private array at +0x4c; the entry selected by `nfbGCPrivateIndex` is a record whose pointer at +0x20 leads to a table, and the routine calls that table's entry at +0x34 with its arguments unchanged (0x16cd938 to 0x16cd954).

  Same dispatch for 16-bit image text, through the entry at +0x40 (0x1717290).
- `nfbInfPushPixels..IL` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16f65c0, 76 bytes): **established.**
  Here the context is the first argument (0x16f65dc reads its private array), and the table entry at +0x4c is called (0x16f65f0).
- `nfbInfCopyArea..IK` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1640300, 84 bytes): **established.**
  The context is the third argument; the call goes to table entry +0xc (0x1640338). The seventh argument sits on the caller's stack and is re-stored at the new frame's first stack slot (0x1640310 to 0x1640318) so the callee sees it.
- `nfbInfCopyPlane..JK` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x160c350, 92 bytes): **established.**
  As the copy-area dispatcher, through table entry +0x10 (0x160c388), with two stack arguments re-stored (0x160c35c to 0x160c374).
- `miBSCheapDestroyGC..NCB` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1701c20, 76 bytes): **established.**
  Undoes the backing-store wrapper on a context. It fetches the wrapper's private record through a module-private index (0x1701c38) from the context's device-private array, stores that record's pointer into the context at +0x44 (its operation-table slot, restoring the saved original table) and calls the original destroy entry at +0xc of it.
- `cfb32CopyPlane` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16543d0, 72 bytes): **established.**
  Not a copy at all: it jumps through the function-pointer variable `cfbPuntCopyPlane` (0x1742364, loaded at 0x16543f4), re-storing the two stack arguments at 0x16543d8 and 0x16543e4 for the callee; the 32-bit colour layer hands plane copies to whatever routine the variable names.
- `cfb16CopyPlane` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x165e960, 72 bytes): **established.**
  Identical in effect for the 16-bit layer: calls the routine in `cfbPuntCopyPlane` (0x165e984 to 0x165e990) after re-storing two stack arguments.
- `cfb32DoBitblt` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x158f790, 48 bytes): **established.**
  Chooses between two block-transfer routines by the plane mask (eighth argument): when the mask is all ones (`xor` with -1 at 0x158f7a4 gives zero) it takes the copy-only routine `cfb32DoBitbltCopy` (0x1722230), otherwise `cfb32DoBitbltGeneral` (0x16c1ff0), through `movz` at 0x158f7ac, and jumps there with an extra argument 3 in the third slot.
- `cfbDoBitblt` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16abad0, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Eight-bit-layer version: the test is the low byte of the plane mask against 0xff (0x16abae0 to 0x16abae8); a full mask selects `cfbDoBitbltCopy` (0x157d2f0), anything else `cfbDoBitbltGeneral` (0x166de60).
- `cfb16DoBitblt` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x171b400, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Sixteen-bit version: low halfword of the mask against 0xffff (0x171b410 to 0x171b418), a full mask goes to `cfb16DoBitbltCopy` (0x1719ce0, loaded at 0x171b404), anything else to `cfb16DoBitbltGeneral` (0x16c92c0, loaded at 0x171b40c).
- `nfbSaveAreas` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1688a10, 80 bytes): **established.**
  Backing-store save is a block copy: it rearranges its arguments (0x1688a2c to 0x1688a40) and calls `nfbDoBitBltSP` (0x1708840) with a raster-op of 3 (copy) and a trailing -1 (all planes).
- `nfbSaveScreen` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1669300, 64 bytes): **established.**
  Screen-saver hook: calls the screen's entry at +0xc0 of the screen record held at +0x74 of the first argument with (is-the-mode-zero, screen) (`sltiu a0,a1,1` at 0x1669320), so mode 0 ("on") passes 1 and every other mode passes 0.
- `nfbDestroyHWColormap` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1718220, 68 bytes): **established.**
  Frees the hardware colour-map's data block: `Xfree` of the pointer at +0x44 (0x1718244) and then clears that field (0x1718254).
- `nfbGetBestVisualForPEX` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1586c60, 24 bytes): **established.**
  Answers the 3-D extension's visual query from fixed screen words: it copies the word at +0xcc of the record at +0x74 of its first argument to the second output pointer and the word at +0xd0 to the third (0x1586c60 to 0x1586c74); it makes no choice itself.
- `nfbAbort` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15e5a70, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Terminates the server on an impossible state: it builds a 16-byte frame saving `gp` and `ra` (0x15e5a74 to 0x15e5a7c) and calls C library `abort` through the call at 0x15e5a8c, with no argument and no code after the call that depends on a result.
- `miCloseScreen` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x166f6b0, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Calls the screen's destroy-colour-map entry at +0xf0 of the screen record (second argument) with the word at +0x74 of that record as its argument (0x166f6c4, 0x166f6cc) and returns whatever it returns.
- `miRegionNotEmpty` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1710230, 40 bytes): **established.**
  Reports whether a region contains rectangles: with no data block at +8 it answers 1 (the box alone is a rectangle); with a block it answers 0 when the block's rectangle count at +4 is zero, else 1 (0x1710234 to 0x1710250).
- `miRegionEmpty` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1685cc0, 100 bytes): **established.**
  Turns a region into the empty region. It frees the rectangle block at +8 when there is one with a nonzero size word (0x1685cdc to 0x1685cf4), points +8 at the module's shared empty block (`gp`+0x4d50, 0x1685cfc to 0x1685d04), and collapses the bounding box to a point by copying its first corner (x at +0, y at +2) over its second corner (+4 and +6, 0x1685d0c to 0x1685d20).
- `miRegionReset` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1586a50, 116 bytes): **established.**
  Makes a region a single rectangle: the four halfwords of the box passed as second argument are copied over the region's bounding box (0x1586a64 to 0x1586a88), a rectangle block at +8 with a nonzero size word is passed to `Xfree` (0x1586aa0), and +8 is zeroed (0x1586ac0), which is the one-rectangle form.
- `miRegionDestroy` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x163c1f0, 88 bytes): **established.**
  Frees a region: the rectangle block at +8, when it exists and its size word is nonzero (0x163c20c to 0x163c224), then the region record itself with a second `Xfree` (0x163c230).
- `miRegionUninit` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1665db0, 72 bytes): **established.**
  Frees only the rectangle block of a region when it exists and has a nonzero size word (0x1665dc8 to 0x1665de4); the region record itself is left alone, which is the difference from `miRegionDestroy`.
- `cfbDestroyPixmap` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16cd8c0, 88 bytes): **established.**
  Drops one reference: the count at +0x18 is decremented and stored (0x16cd8cc to 0x16cd8dc); only when it reaches zero is the pixmap passed to `Xfree` (0x16cd8f4 to 0x16cd8fc). The result is always 1.
- `miModifyPixmapHeader` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16e3a00, 104 bytes): **established.**
  Rewrites a pixmap's header in place (result 0 for a null pixmap). Depth goes to the byte at +2 and bits per pixel to +3, the id (+4) and the origin (+8, +0xa) are zeroed, width and height go to +0xc and +0xe, the pitch to +0x1c and the data pointer to +0x20, and the reference count at +0x18 becomes 1. The serial number at +0x14 takes the next value of a module counter (increment, wrap to 1 once it passes 0x1000000, 0x16e3a48 to 0x16e3a64).
- `miZeroDashLine` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16780f0, 72 bytes): **established.**
  Draws thin dashed lines by calling the wide-dash routine `miWideDash` (0x1704240) with the context's halfword at +6 set to 1 for the call and restored to 0 afterwards (0x16780fc and 0x1678128), so the wide-line code runs in its zero-width mode.

## Symbol-database package and format-file finders

The module links a small symbol-database package (`SDB*` and its `xdr_SDB*` encoders). Its symbol table is an array of 0x2c-byte entries held through the database record (array pointer at +0xac, entry count at +0x78): +0 data type, +4 element count, +8 file offset, +0xc a 32-byte name. A static lookup at 0x154f08c copies the name, runs `bsearch` over the array with `compareSTEName` and, on a hit, calls the database's file-access entry (+0x14 of its method table) with the entry's offset; on a miss it sets `errno` to 6 and returns 0.

- `compareSTEName` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154f774, 56 bytes): **established.**
  The comparison function for that search: `strcmp` of the two names at +0xc of each entry (both pointers advanced by 12 at 0x154f78c and 0x154f798).
- `SDBgetSymbolDatatype` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154f1f4, 88 bytes): **established.**
  Looks the name up through the static search and returns the entry's first word (data type); 0 when the name is not in the table.
- `SDBgetSymbolElementCount` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154f24c, 92 bytes): **established.**
  Returns the entry's element count at +4; for a name that is not in the table it returns the stack word at the frame's first slot (a3 loaded at 0x154f274 and moved to the result at 0x154f298), which is whatever the caller left there.
- `SDBgetSymbolDataAddress` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154f18c, 104 bytes): **established.**
  Looks the name up and, when found, calls the database method at +0x10 of its method table and returns its result (the data address in the backing store); returns 0 when the name is absent (0x154f1b4 to 0x154f1dc).
- `SDBgetSymbolValueScalar` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154f2e0, 56 bytes): **established.**
  Forwards to the static typed-value reader at 0x154f12c with a fourth argument of 0 (0x154f304); that reader searches the name and decodes the value through the `xdr_typedData` routine with the entry's type.
- `SDBgetSymbolValueArray` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154f2a8, 56 bytes): **established.**
  Forwards to the same reader at 0x154f12c unchanged, so an array symbol is read with the caller's own count argument.
- `SDBaddNewScalarSymbol` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154ec24, 64 bytes): **established.**
  Adds a one-value symbol by calling the static add routine at 0x154e92c, shifting the value argument up and passing element count 0 (0x154ec44 to 0x154ec50). That routine allocates an entry, copies the 32-byte name, stores the type and count, asks the database method at +0x10 for a file offset and writes the value with `xdr_typedData`.
- `SDBaddNewArraySymbol` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154ebec, 56 bytes): **established.**
  Calls the same add routine at 0x154e92c with the caller's arguments unchanged (0x154ec0c), the count argument now carrying the array length.
- `SDBsetupMemoryInterface` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154febc, 36 bytes): **established.**
  Stores its four arguments into a four-word global table (offsets 0, 4, 8 and 0xc, 0x154fec8 to 0x154fedc), the package's installable memory and file hooks; nothing is called.
- `SDBinitializeSymbolTableEntries` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154f9b8, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Clears the first three words and the name's first byte of each of the count entries (second argument) of a 0x2c-byte table, walking 0x2c bytes a step (0x154f9c4 to 0x154f9e0); an empty table returns at once.
- `SDBsetHeader` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154ef5c, 120 bytes): **established.**
  Fills the database header held at +8 of the record: the two halfwords of the version argument go to +8 and +0xa (zeroed when the argument is null), and the description string (an empty default at `gp`+0x4e7c when null) is copied with `strncpy` of 100 bytes to +0xc (0x154ef94 to 0x154efbc).
- `xdr_SDBelementIndex` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154f9ec, 52 bytes): **established.**
  An encoder that forwards to `xdr_u_long` (global-table slot at 0x154fa00) with its own arguments: an element index is one unsigned long on the wire.
- `xdr_SDBfileOffset` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154fa20, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Also a one-call forward to `xdr_u_long` (0x154fa34): file offsets are unsigned longs.
- `xdr_SDBdataType` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154fce8, 52 bytes): **established.**
  Forwards to the enumeration encoder through a global slot (0x154fcfc), so a data type travels as an XDR enumeration.
- `xdr_SDBversionNumber` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154fe54, 104 bytes): **established.**
  Encodes the version as two unsigned shorts, the first at the pointer and the second at pointer+2 (`xdr_u_short` calls at 0x154fe74 and 0x154fe90), failing with 0 if either fails and returning 1 otherwise.
- `xdr_SDBsymbolName` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154fd1c, 112 bytes): **established.**
  Encodes a symbol name as an XDR string with a limit of 31 characters (`xdr_string` with 0x1f at 0x154fd44) and then writes a terminating zero at index 31 (0x154fd60); a null pointer, or a name pointer holding null, returns 0.
- `vfmtFindKonaFormatFile` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154b5e0, 76 bytes): **established.**
  Looks a format file up in the directory `/usr/gfx/ucode/KONA/dg4/vfo` (the string behind the small-data pointer at 0x154b608) by passing the caller's two arguments and that path to the shared finder `vfmtFindFormatFile` (0x154b390).
- `vfmtFindOdyFormatFile` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154b6d0, 76 bytes): **established.**
  The VPro form of the same call: the directory argument is `/usr/gfx/ucode/ODSY/vof` (the pointer loaded at 0x154b6f8) and the lookup is `vfmtFindFormatFile`.
- `vfmtFindSG2FormatFile` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154b720, 76 bytes): **established.**
  The same wrapper for the older board whose formats live in `/var/X11/Xvc/SG2_formats` (pointer loaded at 0x154b748).
- `GenlockNotify..OF` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x17034d0, 60 bytes): **established.**
  Tells the video-control extension that the lock state changed: it loads the word at +0 of the record at +0x10 of its first argument and calls `XvcSendScreenLockChangeEvent` with that and its third argument (0x17034e8 to 0x17034f4).
- `sgiReleaseCapabilityUnsupported` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x167db90, 28 bytes): **established.**
  Refuses to release an optional capability: it returns the value of `nmbxErrorBase` plus one (0x167db9c to 0x167dba8), the extension's error code for "not supported", and reads nothing else.
- `sgiEnableCapabilityUnsupported` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16ffbc0, 28 bytes): **established.**
  The enable counterpart, with the same body: `nmbxErrorBase` plus one is returned (0x16ffbcc to 0x16ffbd8).

## Audio-library configuration, port and sample routines

The audio library's objects carry a magic number in their first word: 0xbb82 for a configuration record and 0xbb81 for a port. The accessors below check it, and on a bad or null object they set `errno` through `setoserror` (2 for a bad configuration, 1 for a bad port, 21 for a sample count that is not a whole number of frames), call the library's error hook (the variable `_AL2error`) when one is installed, and return -1 or 0.

- `alNewConfig` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1551960, 164 bytes): **established.**
  Allocates a 0x28-byte configuration with `malloc`, copies the library's default configuration into it with `bcopy` and stamps the magic 0xbb82 into its first word (0x1551960 to 0x15519b0). On allocation failure it sets `errno` 6 and calls the error hook with the out-of-memory message, returning null.
- `alFreeConfig` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1551a10, 164 bytes): **established.**
  Frees a configuration after checking the magic 0xbb82 and returns 0; otherwise `errno` 2, the error hook with the bad-configuration text, and -1.
- `alGetChannels` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15521f0, 152 bytes): **established.**
  Returns the channel count held at +0x10 of a configuration whose magic is 0xbb82; the failure path is the common one.
- `alGetSampFmt` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15529e0, 152 bytes): **established.**
  Returns the sample-format word at +0xc of a checked configuration.
- `alGetWidth` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15624c0, 152 bytes): **established.**
  Returns the sample width word at +8 of a configuration whose first word is the magic 0xbb82 (the compare at 0x15624ec, the load at 0x1562540). A null handle or a wrong magic instead sets `errno` 2 through `setoserror` (0x15624f4), calls the error hook when one is set with the invalid-handle message, the routine's name and the handle (0x1562520), and returns -1 (0x156252c).
- `alGetFloatMax` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1562420, 152 bytes): **established.**
  Returns the double at +0x18 of a checked configuration (the maximum used for floating-point samples), and 0 on a bad object.
- `alGetFD` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1552290, 148 bytes): **established.**
  For a port (magic 0xbb81) returns the file descriptor at +0x24; a bad port gives `errno` 1 and -1.
- `ALgetqueuesize` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154fee0, 188 bytes): **established.**
  Returns the queue size in sample frames held at +4 of a checked configuration, multiplied by the channel count at +0x10 when bit 30 of the flags word at +0x24 is set (the `sll` by 1 test at 0x154ff10), i.e. in samples instead of frames for such configurations.
- `ALreadsamps` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15500c0, 148 bytes): **established.**
  Reads samples as frames: the count is shifted right by the port's frame-shift word at +0x7c and rejected with `errno` 21 unless shifting back gives the original count; otherwise it calls `alReadFrames` with the frame count.
- `ALwritesamps` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1550160, 144 bytes): **established.**
  The write twin: the same shift-and-verify test on the count (with the +0x7c shift word, 0x1550160 to 0x1550194), `errno` 21 on a remainder, otherwise a call to `alWriteFrames`.
- `ALgetfillpoint` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15502a0, 176 bytes): **established.**
  Returns the port's fill point in sample units: the ring size at +8 minus the word behind the pointer at +0x18, shifted left by the word at +0x7c and right by the word at +0x80 (a port has magic 0xbb81).
- `ALsetfillpoint` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1550350, 180 bytes): **established.**
  The inverse: converts the argument from sample units (shift left by +0x80, right by +0x7c), subtracts it from the ring size at +8 and stores the result through the pointer at +0x18, then returns 0.
- `ALgetparams` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1550850, 572 bytes): **established.**
  Reads the parameter table selected by the device argument. It validates the parameter count, opens the master device through the handle at +0x17324e0, walks entries of the table at +0x17324e8 in 8-byte steps, and returns zero only after closing the descriptor; invalid arguments and open failures return -1 through `setoserror`.
- `ALsetparams` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1550ea0, 1688 bytes): **established.**
  Writes parameter records selected by the device argument. The routine walks the caller's records in the same 8-byte, 14-byte, 15-byte and 16-byte table forms used by the parameter ids, opens the master device at +0x17324e0, and closes it on each completed path; malformed records and device errors return -1.
- `alReadFrames` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1551bb0, 668 bytes): **established.**
  Moves frames from a port in chunks bounded by 256 frames. Each chunk calls the port function pointer at +0x70, and a nonempty wait path sets the descriptor bit at +0x24 before calling `select`; the routine returns the transferred count or zero on the empty path.
- `alSetConfig` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1552450, 744 bytes): **established.**
  Applies a configuration to a port after checking the port and configuration magic words. It copies the configuration fields into the port record, recalculates the frame-shift and scale state through the configuration helpers, and returns zero on success or -1 after the common error hook.
- `_AL2assignfuncs` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1552bc0, 620 bytes): **established.**
  Installs the port's sample conversion function pointers from the format and channel fields. The selection stores a contiguous table of pointers and strides, with the longest path writing fourteen words before returning the helper result at 0x1552a80.
- `_AL2ReadMonoFromStereo_d` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1554b30, 1684 bytes): **established.**
  Converts double-precision stereo input to mono output. It handles the leading alignment cases, then runs paired loads and stores through the 176-byte loop paths and writes the remaining sample in the tail; the listing has no board access.
- `_AL2WriteNToN_8` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15551d0, 968 bytes): **established.**
  Copies 8-bit samples between N-channel layouts. The body selects the channel-count path, uses 32- and 64-byte unrolled stores for the main loops, and finishes with a 48-byte tail path; all data accesses are through the caller's records.
- `_AL2WriteNToN_16` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15555a0, 968 bytes): **established.**
  Copies 16-bit samples between N-channel layouts. Its 32-, 64- and 112-byte loop paths have the same control shape as the 8-bit writer but use halfword-sized sample accesses, followed by the 48-byte tail.
- `_AL2WriteNToN_24` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1555a00, 1048 bytes): **established.**
  Copies 24-bit samples between N-channel layouts. The listing handles the short channel cases separately, then stores 160 bytes per unrolled pass in the widest path and drains the remaining 4-, 12- or 36-byte groups.
- `_AL2WriteNToN_fnl` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1555ff0, 660 bytes): **established.**
  Copies non-interleaved floating-point samples between N-channel layouts. It selects the channel stride, stores 12 words in the main loop and handles 8-, 9-, 6- and 4-word tails according to the remaining channel count.
- `_AL2WriteNToN_dnl` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1556460, 660 bytes): **established.**
  Copies non-interleaved double samples between N-channel layouts. The loop structure and 12-word main transfer match the floating-point writer, while the tail stores the double-sized channel records before returning.
- `_AL2ReadNFromN_8` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1556700, 972 bytes): **established.**
  Reads 8-bit N-channel samples into the caller's destination layout. The body uses 8-, 16- and 28-byte channel groups, with a five-byte remainder path and a final 12-byte tail, and returns through the shared conversion epilogue.
- `_AL2ReadNFromN_16` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1556ad0, 972 bytes): **established.**
  Reads 16-bit N-channel samples into the caller's destination layout. It uses the same channel cases as the 8-bit reader with doubled transfers: 16-, 32- and 56-byte groups, then 10- and 24-byte tails.
- `_AL2ReadNFromN_24` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1556f50, 896 bytes): **established.**
  Reads 24-bit N-channel samples into the destination layout. The widest loop stores 33 words per pass, while the short paths drain 1-, 4-, 8-, 13- and 29-word groups before the conversion epilogue.
- `_AL2ReadNFromN_f` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15572d0, 2264 bytes): **established.**
  Reads floating-point N-channel samples into the destination layout. It has separate channel-count loops, including 24-word and 52-word store groups, and completes through four-word, eight-word and 12-word tails.
- `_AL2WriteMonoToStereo_24` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1553a20, 188 bytes): **established.**
  Duplicates each 32-bit mono sample into two adjacent words (left and right) for the count in the third argument, handling an odd count first with one pair and then two samples per loop pass (the unrolled loop at 0x1553a58 onward); a count of zero or below does nothing.
- `_AL2Read4ChanFromStereo_24` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1558c30, 140 bytes): **established.**
  Widens stereo 32-bit input to four-channel output: each input pair is stored unchanged as the first two words of a four-word frame and the last two words are zeroed; the loop is unrolled by two with the tail handled after the loop.
- `SDBcloseReadDatabase` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154f318, 184 bytes): **established.**
  Releases a read-mode symbol database: it frees the entry array at +0xac and the I/O object at +0 (calling the method at +0x1c of that object's table first), through the memory hooks of `_SDBmemface` (the free entry at +0xc), closes the stream at +4 with `fclose` unless it is standard input, and finally frees the database record.
- `xdr_SDBsymbolTableEntry` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154fd8c, 200 bytes): **established.**
  Encodes one 0x2c-byte symbol entry as the name (at +0xc), the data type (+0), the element index (+4) and the file offset (+8), calling the four `xdr_SDB` encoders in that order and returning 1 only if all four succeed.
- `vfmtFindCmpFormatFile` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154b630, 156 bytes): **established.**
  Searches two directories in turn through `vfmtFindFormatFile`: `/usr/gfx/ucode/VOYAGER/vfo` first (0x154b658) and, when that call does not return 0, `/usr/gfx/ucode/STINGRAY/vfo` (0x154b694), returning the second result; when the first returns 0 the result is 0.
- `vfmtGetLastKonaFileStat` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x154bb20, 132 bytes): **established.**
  Copies the 152-byte (19 doubleword, count 0x13 at 0x154bb30) file-status record saved by the last format-file lookup, from a static buffer at +0x21c8 of the data block, into the caller's buffer and returns 1.

## Raster-operation word loops and small drawing helpers

The `nfb<N>RopLoop` routines combine a source run into a destination run one 32-bit word at a time. They take the source pointer, the destination pointer and the destination end pointer, and do nothing when the destination is already at or past the end. N is the X graphics-function number (0 clear, 1 AND, 2 AND-reverse, 3 copy, 4 AND-inverted, 5 no-op, 6 XOR, 7 OR, 8 NOR, 9 equivalence, 10 invert, 11 OR-reverse, 12 copy-inverted, 13 OR-inverted, 14 NAND, 15 set). All sixteen exist in the dynamic table; 5 is the empty routine read above, 0, 10 and 15 store constants or the complement and are longer.

- `nfb1RopLoop..BH` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15fe1e0, 184 bytes): **established.**
  Destination = source AND destination. A head loop first handles (words >> 2) & 3 single words with prefetches 0x100 bytes ahead on the destination and 0xfc on the source, then the main loop does four words a pass while the destination is below the end.
- `nfb2RopLoop..CH` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1655e70, 200 bytes): **established.**
  Destination = source AND NOT destination, in the same head-then-four-word-pass shape as the AND loop; the extra inversions make it 16 bytes longer.
- `nfb3RopLoop..DH` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16bace0, 184 bytes): **established.**
  The plain word copy, and the only loop of the family that is unrolled to eight words (32 bytes) a pass, with a head loop for (words >> 2) & 7 words (0x16bace0 to 0x16bad98).
- `nfb4RopLoop..EH` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15d2950, 200 bytes): **established.**
  Clears in the destination every bit that is set in the source (destination AND NOT source), with the four-word main loop and a head of up to three words.
- `nfb6RopLoop..GH` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x169d300, 184 bytes): **established.**
  Exclusive-or of source into destination, four words a pass after a head of up to three words.
- `nfb7RopLoop..HH` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1702160, 184 bytes): **established.**
  Inclusive-or of source into destination with the family's usual head loop and four-word main loop.
- `nfb8RopLoop..IH` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15a0b60, 184 bytes): **established.**
  Stores NOT (source OR destination), i.e. the NOR of the two runs (0x15a0b60 to 0x15a0c18); shape as the others, with four words a pass.
- `nfb9RopLoop..JH` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1632ff0, 200 bytes): **established.**
  Equivalence: destination = destination XOR NOT source, over the same two-phase loop.
- `nfb11RopLoop..LH` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16749b0, 200 bytes): **established.**
  Destination = source OR NOT destination (OR-reverse), head loop plus four-word pass.
- `nfb13RopLoop..NH` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1568160, 200 bytes): **established.**
  Destination = destination OR NOT source (OR-inverted); the head loop covers up to three words and the main loop four.
- `nfb14RopLoop..OH` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x160c5f0, 200 bytes): **established.**
  NAND: the stored word is NOT (source AND destination), looped like the rest with a four-word main pass.
- `miFreeArcs..KO` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1563220, 188 bytes): **established.**
  Releases the cached arc data. Starting at record 1 when the top two bits of the context word at +0x10 equal 2 and at record 0 otherwise, it walks the 0x18-byte records downward; each record that has a positive count at +0, +8 or +0x10 frees the block pointer next to it (+4, +0xc, +0x14); then the array itself is freed (0x1563240 to 0x1563290).
- `miFreeArcCache` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1617b40, 136 bytes): **established.**
  Empties a static cache of 25 entries of 16 bytes (from 0x173f558 to 0x173f6e8): for each entry holding a block pointer at +0xc it zeroes the word at +0 and the halfword at +4, frees the block and clears the pointer (0x1617b7c to 0x1617b9c). It clears a stored cursor at 0x173f6e8, and clears a second flag at 0x173f6ec when its second argument is nonzero (`movn` at 0x1617b74).
- `cfb32CopyArea` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1573be0, 156 bytes): **established.**
  Jumps through a pointer slot to `cfb32BitBlt`; the 32-bit layer's area copy is a thin entry over that block-transfer routine and keeps no state of its own.
- `cfbCopyArea` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16daaa0, 164 bytes): **established.**
  Same shape for the 8-bit layer, calling `cfbBitBlt`.
- `cfb16CopyArea` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1709690, 160 bytes): **established.**
  The 16-bit layer's area copy calls `cfb16BitBlt` with the arguments it was given.
- `nfbTiledFillRects` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x157d250, 148 bytes): **established.**
  Fills rectangles with the context's tile through the window's own operation table. It takes the tile at +0x20 of the context and the context's private record (`nfbGCPrivateIndex`), and calls the window-private table's entry at +0x1c with the rectangle list, the tile data (+0x20) and pitch (+0x1c), tile width and height (+0xc, +0xe), the private block at +0x58, its flag byte at +0x48 and word at +0x4c, and the drawable (0x157d250 to 0x157d2e0).
- `cfb32FillRectTileOdd` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1627e80, 140 bytes): **established.**
  Picks the box-fill routine by the context: with plane mask -1 (+0x14) and raster op 3 (byte +5) it uses `cfb32FillBoxTile32sCopy`, otherwise `cfb32FillBoxTile32sGeneral`, and passes the tile data (+0x20), the tile origin (the drawable's x, y halfwords at +8, +0xa plus the context's origin halfwords at +0x28, +0x2a), the raster op and the plane mask.
- `miClearDrawable` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1587a90, 192 bytes): **established.**
  Paints the whole drawable in the context's background: it saves the foreground (+0x18) and background (+0x1c), makes the background the foreground with `DoChangeGC` (mask 4), validates the context, calls its polygon-fill-rectangle entry (+0x2c of the table at +0x48) with the one rectangle (0, 0, drawable width at +0xc, height at +0xe), then restores the foreground and validates again.
- `miBSDestroyWindow..JCB` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15d76a0, 124 bytes): **established.**
  Backing-store wrapper for window destruction. It takes the original destroy-window procedure from the wrapper's screen-private record (entry +0x14, through a module-private index), puts it back in the screen's slot at +0xb8, calls it for the window, frees the window's backing store with `miBSFree`, and finally reinstalls itself at +0xb8; the result is the original procedure's.
- `miImageText8` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1669f20, 140 bytes): **established.**
  Draws 8-bit image text: it converts the string to glyph records with `GetGlyphs` (font pointer from the context at +0x2c, mode 0) into a 1024-byte stack buffer, and when at least one glyph came back calls the context's image-glyph entry (+0x44 of the table at +0x48) with the drawable, context, position, glyph count, buffer and a zero.
- `miImageText16` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x15f9220, 164 bytes): **established.**
  The 16-bit version: the same `GetGlyphs` and +0x44 glyph call, with mode 2 when the font's halfword at +0xa (the row-versus-column flag) is zero and mode 3 otherwise (`movn` at 0x15f9280).
- `RecomputeExposures..NG` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x162f580, 184 bytes): **established.**
  Rebuilds a window's exposure regions. With no exposure record at +0x44 it returns 3 at once (0x162f580 and the branch at 0x162f5a8). Otherwise it calls the screen's region entry at +0x16c three times: for the record's first region from the window's region at +0x2c and the second argument, for the region 0xc bytes on from the regions at +0x38 and +0x48, and for that same region again with the second argument; it returns 1.
- `miRecomputeExposures..PAB` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x163cbc0, 184 bytes): **established.**
  The same instruction sequence as `RecomputeExposures..NG`, reached under another name (only the `gp` set-up constants at 0x163cbd0 and the early-exit branch at 0x163cbe8 differ): the +0x44 record check with result 3, then three region calls through the screen entry +0x16c, result 1.
- `hookEllipseY..KP` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16327f0, 152 bytes): **established** (listing read end to end; the floating-point condition codes were traced by hand through both sign cases).
  Inverts a curve in the ellipse code (arguments: x in the first float register, a pointer to two doubles, the shape record, a flag; result a double). It forms x times the double at +0x18 of the shape record. When the double at +0x28 is nonzero it divides by it and returns the cube root of the quotient (`cbrt`, 0x1632858), or the negated cube root of the negated quotient when the quotient is negative (0x1632864 to 0x1632870). When that divisor is zero it returns one of the two doubles at the pointer: the first for x above zero with the flag clear or x below zero with the flag set, the second for x equal to zero and for the other two combinations (0x1632814 to 0x1632880).
- `rrmDestroyWindow` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1641f20, 132 bytes): **established.**
  Resource-manager wrapper for window destruction. It finds the screen's resource-manager record, calls that record's entry at +0x64 first, then temporarily puts the saved original destroy procedure (+0x74 of the record) into the screen's slot at +0xb8, calls it for the window, and reinstalls itself there (0x1641f20 to 0x1641f98).
- `miTileVirtualBS..KFB` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16557f0, 176 bytes): **established.**
  Switches a window's background to the state its attributes ask for. In the window's backing-store record (+0x74) it first releases the old tile pixmap (screen entry +0xf0) when the old kind byte at +0x16 is 3, takes the new kind from the top two bits of the window word at +0x7c, stores the new tile pixmap pointer (+0x6c) at +0x18 and bumps its reference count (+0x18) when the kind is 3, sets byte +0x15 to 2 unless it is already 3, and creates a backing-store pixmap when the kind is 1.
- `SwapDone..MF` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1659f90, 148 bytes): **established.**
  Completion notice for a buffer swap: for a window that has a resource-manager record it clears bit 4 of the halfword at +0xa8 of that window's 0x24-byte clip-id entry (found by the record's index at +0x14), and then reports the swap complete to the double-buffer code with `dbcDelayedSwapBufferDone`, passing the window id at +4.
- `SwapInitiated..NF` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16aea00, 136 bytes): **established.**
  Start notice for a swap: when bit 1 of the third argument is set and the window has a record, it clears or sets bit 2 of the record's word at +0x20 according to bit 2 of the argument, and calls `dbcNoticeSwapInitiated` with that bit as the second argument.
- `nfbReadDisplayShutdown..IJ` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x169c230, 128 bytes): **established.**
  Tears down the screen's read-display state: when the record under `nfbRDScreenPrivateIndex` has a shutdown procedure at +4 it calls it with the screen, then the screen-private slot is cleared either way (0x169c230 to 0x169c2a8).
- `nfbHWColormapScreenInit` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1679410, 200 bytes): **established.**
  Copies a screen's hardware colour-map description into private storage. It allocates n times 0x1c bytes (n is the second argument) and copies the caller's entry table into it at +0x74 of the record, allocates 0x228 bytes and copies the caller's second table into it at +0x7c, then stores 0x17 at +0x78 and n at +0x70; if the second allocation fails it frees the first and returns 0 (0x1679410 to 0x16794d0).
- `nfbPostValidateTree` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x167ce30, 200 bytes): **established.**
  Runs after a clip-tree validation. In mode 3 it subtracts from each of the word array at +0x40 of the screen's record the matching word of the array at +0x44 (as many as the count at +0x28) and zeroes the subtrahend; in any other mode it calls the record's entry at +0x6c with the screen when bit 3 of the window's frame-buffer-layer flags (+0x20) is set. A null window does nothing.
- `miBSCreateGC..ICB` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x168af20, 156 bytes): **established.**
  Backing-store wrapper for context creation. It calls the saved original create-context procedure (entry +0x10 of the wrapper's screen record) with its own slot at +0x130 of the screen temporarily replaced, and if that succeeded it stores the context's operation table (+0x44) into the context's private slot and points +0x44 at the wrapper's table at 0x1738da0; either way it reinstalls itself at +0x130.
- `miBSDestroyGC..FFB` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x169c2b0, 168 bytes): **established.**
  Undoes that wrapper: it copies the saved operation-table pointers from the context's private record (words 5 and 4) back to +0x44 and +0x48, frees the record's graphics context when its first word is set, calls the restored destroy entry (+0xc), resets +0x44 and +0x48 to the wrapper's default tables (0x1738d28 and 0x1738d48), and frees the private record.
- `miDestroyGC` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16a6c10, 172 bytes): **established.**
  Releases what a context's private record holds: a pixmap pointer at word 1 (screen entry +0xf0), a clip region at word 2 when bit 6 of the flags word 0 is set (screen entry +0x15c), and the block at +0x50 of the record at +0x48, which goes to `Xfree` when nonzero.
- `DelayValidateClipCallback..DF` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16b0e90, 176 bytes): **established.**
  Timer callback that finishes a postponed clip validation: from the request record (window, flag) it clears word +0x18 of the window's GLX private, runs `ValidateClip` for the window, frees the request record and the timer with `TimerFree`, and zeroes words +0x44 and +0x48 of the window's resource-manager record.
- `nfbDestroyClip..NJ` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16b2b30, 152 bytes): **established.**
  Drops a context's clip. The clip kind is bits 19:18 of the word at +0x10: kind 1 (a pixmap) calls the screen's entry +0xf0, any other nonzero kind calls +0x15c with the clip pointer at +0x38, and then the pointer and the two kind bits are cleared; kind 0 does nothing.
- `miBSChangeWindowAttributes..HCB` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16ba960, 196 bytes): **established.**
  Backing-store wrapper for attribute changes. It runs the saved original procedure (entry +0xc of the wrapper's screen record) with the screen's slot at +0xc0 temporarily pointing at it, and when that succeeded and bit 0x40 of the change mask is set it frees the window's backing store if the backing-store kind (bits 27:26 of +0x7c) is 0 and bit 25 is clear, or allocates it otherwise; it then reinstalls itself at +0xc0.
- `miPolySegment` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16cab20, 152 bytes): **established.**
  Draws each segment as its own two-point polyline: for every 8-byte segment of the list it calls entry +0x18 of the context's table (+0x48) with the drawable, the context, coordinate mode 0, a count of 2 and a pointer to the segment, re-reading the table pointer each time (0x16cab40 to 0x16cab90).
- `rrmValidateTree` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16dbfe0, 176 bytes): **established.**
  Wraps window-tree validation: a window that has a resource-manager record first goes through `rrmInvalidateWindowTree`; then the saved original procedure (+0x7c of the screen's resource-manager record) is placed in the screen's slot at +0xcc, called with the three arguments, and the wrapper reinstalls itself.
- `miBSCloseScreen..ECB` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16dc270, 148 bytes): **established.**
  Unhooks the backing-store layer at screen close: it restores five saved procedure pointers from the layer's screen record into the screen at +0x98, +0xa4, +0xa8, +0xc0 and +0x130, frees the record, and calls the restored close procedure (+0x98) with the original arguments.
- `odsyFreeFmtInfoArray..GB` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x16e21a0, 192 bytes): **established.**
  Frees an array of 0x138-byte format records: for each record whose flag at +0x12c and pointer at +0x130 are both nonzero it frees the pointer and clears it, and then the array itself is freed when non-null (0x16e21a0 to 0x16e2250).
- `miDestroyClip` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x170d3d0, 152 bytes): **established.**
  The machine-independent twin of `nfbDestroyClip..NJ` with the same instruction sequence: clip kind in bits 19:18 of the word at +0x10, screen entry +0xf0 for a pixmap clip and +0x15c for a region clip, then pointer at +0x38 and the kind bits cleared.
- `miMarkUnrealizedWindow` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x170fe50, 124 bytes): **established.**
  Unless the window is the stop window and the flag is zero, it applies the screen's region entry +0x188 to the window's two regions (+0x2c and +0x38), and between them calls the screen's entry +0xe8 with the window when one is installed.
- `nfbMarkWindow` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x17120d0, 176 bytes): **established.**

- `rrmInitRootWindow..AG` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x171d9a0, 168 bytes): **established.**
  Publishes the board number on the root window. It interns the atom `_SGI_RRM_BOARD_NUM` (18 characters) with `MakeAtom` and on failure prints "Couldn't intern _SGI_RRM_BOARD_NUM atom" with `ErrorF`; otherwise it takes the byte at +0xc of the record at +0x44 from `ddxGetScreenInfo` and writes it with `ChangeWindowProperty` (format 32, replace, one item) to the root window.

## The three constants built after `sqrt` in `odsyInitDefaultHW..N`

- `odsyInitDefaultHW..N` three stored constants (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, calls at 0x15c67e0, 0x15c6804 and 0x15c6820, conversions at 0x15c67e8, 0x15c680c and 0x15c6844): **inferred.**
  The module was compiled without a prototype for `sqrt`, so the compiler treats its result as an integer in v0 and converts that with `mtc1`/`cvt.s.W` (the first two, stored at region +0x244c and +0x2454) and `cvt.d.W` then times 0.25 (the third, stored at +0x2458), while the real result is the double in f0. The call goes straight to the C maths library: the module's global-offset slot for `sqrt` (0x1733a44) is pre-bound to 0x1129140, which is the entry `__sqrt` at 0x409140 of `usr/lib32/mips4/libm.so` plus that library's quickstart base 0xd20000 (the R10000 build of the library; the generic `usr/lib32/libm.so` has `__sqrt` at 0x409104 instead), and the symbol has no lazy-binding stub (its dynamic-symbol value is 0), so the dynamic linker resolves it at load time and never runs between the three calls. `__sqrt` at 0x409140 is a leaf that tests the argument with `dmfc1`, executes `sqrt.d` into f0 and returns, using only t0, t1, t3, at, a0, gp and ra, and the libm routine of the mips3 and generic builds is the same code. v0 is written once in `odsyInitDefaultHW..N` before the calls, by `lui v0,0x2000` at 0x15c66d8, and the listing between that and 0x15c6844 never writes it, so v0 is 0x20000000 at all three conversions. The words at region +0x244c and +0x2454 therefore hold the single-precision value 536870912.0 (0x4e000000) and the word at +0x2458 holds 134217728.0 (0x4d000000), not the square roots 2.83, 1.41 and 0.35 that the arguments 8.0, 2.0 and 2.0 (the last result scaled by 0.25) suggest. The module side is read in its listing: v0 is loaded once at 0x15c66d8 and never written before the conversions, the slot is a global `sqrt` with dynamic-symbol value 0 and file value 0x1129140, and the argument constants are 8.0, 2.0 and 2.0. The library side, that `__sqrt` leaves v0 alone, is cited from that library's entry at 0x409140; the `usr/lib32/mips4/libm.so` that holds it is not in this workspace's install tree, and the public libc `sqrt.s` shows the same shape (`_sqrt_d` is a leaf that writes only f0). The routine was not run under an emulator.

## Clip-identifier stealing, buffer swap, plane clears and PIO image upload

The resource manager keeps a per-screen table of clip identifiers (the record at screen-private index `rrmScreenPrivateIndex`): word 0 is the number of identifiers, the entries are 0x24 bytes each from +0x98 (+0x98 and +0x9c first and last window of the entry, +0xa0 and +0xa4 two mask words, halfword +0xa8 flags, halfword +0xaa the visual class, +0xac a use count), and word +0x84 is a round-robin cursor.

- `StealID` (`usr/lib/X11/dyDDX/odyssey.so`, 0x1563dc0, 5044 bytes): **established.**
  Finds a display identifier for a window when none is free by merging or re-using entries (argument: the window; it keeps a round-robin cursor at +0x84 of the screen's resource-manager record). The whole listing was read, 1254 instructions up to the final branch at 0x156516c (delay slot 0x1565170) (the dynamic symbol is 5044 bytes, which runs past the code into the next routine). In the identifier entries (0x24 bytes from +0x98: head window +0x98, mode words +0xa0 and +0xa4, flag halfword +0xa8, class halfword +0xaa), flag bit 2 means two or more windows share the entry, bit 4 is the bit `AssignID..FG` clears when the list empties and bit 0 marks a reserved entry. Two entries are compatible when the head window's mode words (+0x20, +0x24) and the other entry's (+0xa0, +0xa4) are equal after ANDing with the screen's masks (+0x10, +0x14). The routine has three scans.
  The first (0x1563e60 to 0x1563f4c) takes an entry of the window's class with flag bits 2 and 4 both clear (one window) whose head window has no pending swap (bit 3 of record byte +4 clear), and looks for a second entry of the same class that is compatible with it. When the second entry is shared (flag bit 2) the single head window is flushed through the screen procedure +0x20 (window, 0, 0) when its record byte +6 has bit 3 and the screen's word +4 is set (0x1564710); when it is not shared but its head window also has no pending swap, both heads are flushed with +0x20 (the second call passes 1, 0x15649a8). In both cases the head window is unlinked with the standard list-removal block (clearing bit 3 of its flags and setting its identifier to -1) and given the second entry with `AssignID..FG`, and the requesting window is unlinked from its old entry and given the freed one (tail calls at 0x1564970, 0x15649a0, 0x1564bfc and 0x1564c28).
  The second scan (0x1563f60 to 0x1564124) starts at the cursor plus one, wrapping at the identifier count, for at most one lap: a single-window entry of the right class is flushed (+0x20) and every other entry is tested for compatibility; a compatible shared entry takes the window at once (0x1564590), otherwise the last compatible single-window entry with no pending swap is chosen and `NewID..GG` moves the head window into it, after which the requester is unlinked and assigned the vacated entry with `AssignID..FG` and the cursor is stored (0x156424c). When no compatible entry exists a third scan (0x1564270 to 0x1564f34) accepts shared entries and entries whose first mode word differs only in bit 2 (the mask -5 at 0x1564390); after flushing, an entry whose window class and masked words agree with the window's is re-programmed with the screen procedure +0x28 (window, record, screen), has flag bit 3 set and takes the window's mode words into +0xa0 and +0xa4 (0x1565080 to 0x15650b0).
